questions.question: A service catalog may include which of the following components?
options: Order Guides, Catalog Items, and Interceptors
Catalog Items, Asset Contracts, Task Surveys
Record Producers, Order Guides, and Catalog Items
questions.explanation: A Service Catalog is assembled from Catalog Items (the orderable products and services), Order Guides (which bundle several related items into a single guided request), and Record Producers (catalog-style forms that create records on a target table). Option D names all three. The other choices fold in unrelated platform features such as Exchange Rates, Calendars, Asset Contracts, and Task Surveys, none of which are catalog building blocks.

questions.question: Which one of the following statements applies to a set of fields when they are coalesced during an import?
options: If a match is found using the coalesce fields, the existing record is updated with the information being imported
If a match is not found using the coalesce fields, the system does not create a Transform Map
If a match is found using the coalesce fields, the system creates a new record
If a match is not found using the coalesce fields, the existing record is updated with the information being imported
questions.explanation: The coalesce fields serve as the match key during a transform. When the system finds an existing record whose coalesce value equals the incoming row, it updates that record rather than inserting a duplicate (A). If no match exists it inserts a new record, so options C and D have the logic reversed, and coalescing has no bearing on whether a Transform Map is created (B).
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Field mapping and coalesce

questions.question: As it relates to ServiceNow reporting, which of the following statements describes what a metric can do?
options: A metric is a report gauge used on homepages to display real-time data
A metric is a time measurement used to report the effectiveness of workflows and SLAs
A metric is used to measure and evaluate the effectiveness of IT service management processes
A metric is a comparative measurement used to report the effectiveness of workflows and SLAs.
questions.explanation: A Metric measures and evaluates how effective and efficient your ITSM processes are over time, such as how long a record spends in a given state (C). A gauge (A) is a homepage visualization rather than the metric itself, and options B and D describe SLA behavior, not what a metric does.

questions.question: The display Sequence is controlled in a service catalog item using which of the following?
options: The Default Value field in the Catalog Item form
The Sequence field in the Catalog Item form
The Order field in the Variable form
The Choice field in the Variable form
questions.explanation: The order in which variables appear on a catalog item is governed by the Order field on each Variable record; lower Order values render higher on the form (C). The Default Value field seeds a starting value, the Choice field defines selectable options for choice-type variables, and there is no Sequence field on the Catalog Item form that drives variable display order.

questions.question: Reports can be created from which different places in the platform? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: A report can be generated straight from a list column heading by clicking the header and choosing a chart/create-report option (A), and from the Reports application using the View / Run module, which opens the report designer (D). The Metrics and Statistics modules (B and C) are not entry points for building reports.

questions.question: Knowledge base search results can be sorted by which of the following? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Knowledge search results can be sorted by Relevancy (best keyword match), Most recent update (newest content), and Number of views (most-read articles) - A, C, and E. 'Popularity' and 'Manager assignment' are not standard Knowledge search sort options.

questions.question: What is the path an administrator could take to view the fulfillment stage task list for an order placed by a user?
questions.explanation: Placing an order creates a Request (REQ). Each REQ holds one or more Requested Items (RITM), and every RITM spawns the catalog Tasks (TASK) that fulfillers actually work. The administrator therefore drills REQ to RITM to TASK (C). 'Procurement' and 'Fulfillment' are not records in this chain.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Service Catalog request fulfillment

questions.question: Which term refers to application menus and modules which you may want to access quickly and often?
questions.explanation: Application menus and modules you want to reach quickly are saved as Favorites, accessible from the star/favorites view in the Application Navigator (B). A Bookmark is a browser-level concept, a Breadcrumb shows your filter path on a list, and a Tag labels records, so none of those is the navigator shortcut described.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Favorites in the navigator

questions.question: What is generated from the service catalog once a user places an order for an item or service?
questions.explanation: Submitting a catalog order generates a Request (REQ), the top-level record that tracks the overall order and contains the individual Requested Items (C). An Order Guide is a tool used before ordering to bundle items, a change request belongs to Change Management, and an SLA tracks timeliness rather than being created by placing an order.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Requests, items, and tasks

questions.question: From the user menu, which actions can a user select? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: From the user/settings menu in the top-right banner a user can Log Out, Elevate Roles (temporarily activate elevated privileges such as security_admin), and Impersonate Users (admins acting as another user for testing) - B, C, and D. Sending notifications, ordering from the catalog, and approving records are performed elsewhere in the platform, not from this menu.

questions.question: Buttons, form links, and context menu items are all examples of what type of functionality?
questions.explanation: Buttons, form links, and context-menu items are all configured as UI Actions, which place clickable controls in the interface that run server- or client-side logic (B). Business Rules execute on the server during database operations, Client Scripts react to form events, and UI Policies dynamically change field state, so none of them renders those clickable controls.

questions.question: Which of the following is true of service catalog items in relation to the service catalog?
questions.explanation: Catalog Items are the fundamental building blocks of a Service Catalog; they are the orderable products and services that users actually request (B). They are visible front-end records rather than something that runs behind the scenes, they are not optional to a functioning catalog, and 'provide options' more accurately describes variables within an item.

questions.question: Table access control rules are processed in the following order:
options: any table name (wildcard), parent table name, table name
table name, parent table name, any table name (wildcard)
parent table name, table name, any table name (wildcard)
any table name (wildcard), table name, parent table name
questions.explanation: ServiceNow evaluates matching ACLs from most specific to least specific: the table's own ACL first, then ACLs on its parent table(s), and finally the wildcard (*) 'any table' rule - order B. Because access requires passing the most specific applicable rule, specificity is checked before the catch-all wildcard.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - How access control rules are processed

questions.question: What is the platform name for the user table?
questions.explanation: The platform (database) name of the User table is sys_user (D), singular and carrying the sys_ prefix used for core platform tables. 'sys_users' is wrong because it is plural, while the u_ and x_ prefixes denote custom tables in the global and scoped applications respectively, not the core User table.

questions.question: A req number in the service catalog represents"
options: the individual item in the order.
questions.explanation: A REQ (Request) number represents the overall order a user places (A). Within that request, each Requested Item (RITM) is an individual item in the order, and catalog Tasks (TASK) track the work to complete it, so 'the individual item' and 'the task' describe RITM and TASK rather than REQ.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Requests, items, and tasks

questions.question: Which would not appear in the history section of the application navigator?
questions.explanation: The History section of the Application Navigator records the lists, forms, and individual records a user has recently visited, so it surfaces Records, Lists, and Forms. UI Pages are standalone Jelly/HTML pages that are not tracked as navigation history, which is why B is the item that would NOT appear.

questions.question: Which one of the following statements is a recommendation from ServiceNow about update sets?
options: Avoid using the Default Update set as an Update Set for moving customizations from instance to instance
Before moving customizations from instance to instance with Update Sets, ensure that both instances are different versions
Use the Baseline Update Set to store the contents of items after they are changed the first time
Once an Update Set is closed as 'Complete', change it back to 'In Progress' until it is applied to another instance
questions.explanation: ServiceNow recommends not using the Default update set to move customizations between instances (A); leave Default in place and create named update sets for your work. The others are anti-patterns: source and target instances should be on the same version, a Completed set should not be reopened, and the Baseline set is a system-managed record used for back-out rather than a place you store changes.

questions.question: Which of the following is used to initiate a flow?
questions.explanation: Every Flow Designer flow begins with a Trigger, which defines the condition that starts the flow, such as a record being created or updated, a schedule, or an inbound email (A). Core Actions are steps inside the flow, a Spoke is a packaged set of integration actions, and an Event is a separate, legacy automation mechanism.

questions.question: For administrators creating new service catalog items, what is a characteristic they should know about service catalog variables?
options: Service Catalog variables can only be used in Record Producers
Service Catalog variables can only be used in Order Guides
Service Catalog variables cannot affect the order price
Service Catalog variables are global by default
questions.explanation: The source answer marks D, treating variables as global by default. In practice this is misleading: each variable is owned by a single catalog item unless it is deliberately created as a Variable Set and shared, and price-affecting variables (such as pricing on a choice) directly contradict option C. Options A and B are clearly false because variables are used across catalog items generally, not solely in Record Producers or Order Guides.

questions.question: Which one of the following statements is true about column context menus?
options: It displays actions such as creating quick reports, configuring the list, and exporting data
It displays actions related to filtering options, assigning tags, and search
It displays actions related to viewing and filtering the entire list
It displays actions such as view form, view related task, and add relationship
questions.explanation: The column context menu, opened by clicking a list column heading, exposes actions for working with the displayed data such as creating quick reports, configuring the list, grouping, and exporting (A). Viewing a related form or record and 'add relationship' belong to the row/record context menu, not the column header menu.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - List column context menu

questions.question: Which one statement correctly describes access control rule evaluation?
options: Rules are evaluated using roles. The role with the most permissions evaluates the rules first
If more than one rule applies to a row, the older rule is evaluated first
If a row level rule and a field level rule exist, both rules must be true before an operation is allowed
Rules are evaluated from the general to the specific, so a table rule must be active to continue
questions.explanation: For a given operation ServiceNow evaluates both the table/row-level ACL and the more specific field-level ACL, and the user must pass BOTH before access is granted (option C). Option D is wrong because ACLs are matched most-specific to most-general (specific-to-general), not 'general to the specific.' Options A and B misstate the algorithm: evaluation order is not based on which role has the most permissions, nor on rule age.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Access control rule evaluation

questions.question: When using the load data and transform map process, what is the mapping Assist used for?
options: Mapping fields using the Import Log
Mapping fields using a Field Map
questions.explanation: Mapping Assist is the visual tool that lets you create field maps by pairing source columns to target fields, so it maps fields using a Field Map (D). The Import Log and Transform History are diagnostic records of what happened during a load, and an SLA is unrelated to field mapping entirely.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Mapping fields with Mapping Assist

questions.question: Which one of the following statements describes the contents of the configuration management database (CMDB)?
options: The CMDB contains data about tangible and intangible business assets
The CMDB contains the Business Rules that direct the intangible, configurable assets used by a company
The CMDB archives all Service Management PaaS equipment metadata and usage statistics
The CMDB contains ITIL process data pertaining to configuration items
questions.explanation: The CMDB stores configuration items (CIs), which span both tangible assets such as servers and laptops and intangible ones such as business services and applications (A). It does not hold Business Rules (B), it is not merely an archive of PaaS equipment statistics (C), and it stores CI data rather than ITIL process records themselves (D).

questions.question: In what order should filter elements be specified?
questions.explanation: A filter condition is built in the order Field, Operator, then Value, for example 'Priority' 'is' '1 - Critical' (A). The other sequences scramble these elements; 'Condition' is the whole expression rather than a standalone third element, and reversing to Value-first does not match how the con‐ dition builder accepts input.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Filters and the condition builder

questions.question: Which statement is true about business rules?
options: A business rule must run before a database action occurs
A business rule can be a piece of Javascript
A business rule must not run before a database action occurs
A business rule monitors fields on a form
questions.explanation: A Business Rule is server-side logic written in JavaScript that runs when records are queried, inserted, updated, or deleted (B). It can be configured to run before, after, async, or on display relative to the database action, so 'must run before' and 'must not run before' are both false, and monitoring fields on a form as a user types is the job of Client Scripts and UI Policies.

questions.question: Which of the following are a type of client scripts supported in ServiceNow? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: ServiceNow supports four client script types: onLoad (runs when the form loads), onChange (runs when a specified field changes), onSubmit (runs when the form is submitted), and onCell‐ Edit (runs when a field is edited inline in a list) - A, C, D, and F. onUpdate, onEdit, and onSave are not valid client script types.

questions.question: Which type of tables may be extended by other tables, but do not extend another table?
questions.explanation: A Base Table sits at the top of a class hierarchy: other tables can extend it, but it does not itself extend a parent (A). Extended Tables are by definition children that inherit from a parent, Core Tables refers broadly to ServiceNow's built-in tables, and Custom Tables are simply tables an admin creates, which may or may not extend something.

questions.question: Which of the following statement describes the purpose of an order guide?
options: Order Guides restrict the number of items in an order to only one item per request
Order Guide provide a list of guidelines for Administrators on how to set up item variables
Order Guide provide the ability to order multiple, related items as one request
Order Guides take the user directly to the checkout without prompting for information
questions.explanation: An Order Guide lets a user order multiple related items together as a single request, often gathering shared information once and using it to populate each included item (C). This is the opposite of restricting an order to one item (A), it is a user-facing ordering tool rather than admin guidelines (B), and it adds a guided flow rather than skipping straight to checkout (D).

questions.question: Which tool is used to have conversations with logged-in users in real-time?
questions.explanation: Connect Chat provides real-time messaging between logged-in users, supporting one-to-one and group conversations inside the platform (A). User Presence only indicates whether someone is online, Comments are an asynchronous journal field on records, and Now Messenger refers to the Virtual Agent end-user chat widget rather than person-to-person chat.

questions.question: Which of the following concepts are associated with the ServiceNow CMDB? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: The CMDB is associated with a Database of configuration items, the Tables and Fields that model those CIs, the Service Processes the CIs support, and the Dependency View that visualizes CI relationships - A, C, D, and E. User Permissions are governed by roles and ACLs, which are a separate security concern rather than a CMDB concept.

questions.question: What is a formatter?
options: A formatter allows you to configure applications on your instance
A formatter is a form element used to display information that is not a field in the record
A formatter allows you to populate fields automatically
A formatter is a set of conditions applied to a table to help find and work with data
questions.explanation: A formatter is a form element that displays information not stored directly as a field on the record, such as an Activity stream or an Approvers summary (B). Automatically populating fields is the job of scripts or defaults (C), and a set of conditions applied to a table to find data describes a filter (D), not a formatter.

questions.question: When searching using the app navigator search field, what can be returned? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: Typing in the Application Navigator filter narrows the navigation tree by matching application names, module names, the combination of both, and favorites - A, B, C, and D. It filters the navigator content, so it does not return browsing History records or the titles of dashboard gauges.

questions.question: Which technique is used to get information from a series of referenced fields from different tables?
questions.explanation: Dot-walking follows reference fields from one table to another using dot notation, for example caller_id.department.name, to reach values on related records (C). 'Table-Walking', 'Sys_ID Pulling', and 'Record-Hopping' are not ServiceNow terms and are included only as distractors.

questions.question: What is a schema map?
options: A schema map enables administrators to define records from specific tables as trouble sources for Configuration Items
A schema map graphically organizes the visual task boards for the CMDB
A schema map graphically displays the Configuration Items that support a business service
A schema map displays the details of tables and their relationships in a visual manner, allowing administrators to view and easily access different parts of the database schema
questions.explanation: A schema map visually displays tables and the relationships between them, letting administrators explore and navigate the database schema (D). Graphically displaying the CIs that support a business service describes a dependency/business service map (C), and the other options invent unrelated trouble-source or task-board behavior.

questions.question: Which one of the following statements best describes the purpose of an update set?
options: An Update Set allows administrators to group a series of changes into a named set and then move this set as a unit to other systems
By default, an Update Set includes customizations, Business Rules, and homepages
An Update Set is a group of customizations that is moved from Production to Development
By default, the changes included in an Update Set are visible only in the instance to which they are applied
questions.explanation: An Update Set groups a series of configuration changes into a named bundle that can be moved as a single unit to other instances (A). Update Sets normally promote changes from a lower environment such as Development up to Production, not the reverse (C), and the remaining options misstate default contents and visibility.

questions.question: Which of the following can be customized through the Basic Configuration UI 16 module? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The Basic Configuration (UI16) module lets administrators set branding and global preferences such as the Banner Image, the Browser Tab Title, and the System Date Format - A, C, and D. Record Number Format is configured per table on the Number record, and there is no Form Header Size setting in this module.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Branding and Basic Configuration (UI16)

questions.question: What is the function of user impersonation?
questions.explanation: Impersonation lets an administrator act as another user to test what that user can see and do, which is invaluable for verifying roles, ACLs, and the self-service experience (A). It does not enable verbose logging, render special perspectives, or unlock any application master list.

questions.question: What information does the system dictionary contain?
options: The human-readable labels and language settings
The definition for each table and column
The information on how tables relate to each other
The language dictionary used for spell checking
questions.explanation: The System Dictionary (sys_dictionary) stores the definition of every table and field, including data type, length, and attributes (B). Human-readable labels live in the related Field Labels (sys_documentation) table (A), table relationships are modeled separately through references and the schema map (C), and it has nothing to do with spell-check dictionaries (D).

questions.question: When working on a form, what is the difference between insert and update operations?
options: Insert creates a new record and Update saves changes, both remain on the form
Insert creates a new record and Update saves changes, both exit the form
Insert saves changes and exits the form, Update saves changes and remains on the form
Insert saves changes and remains on the form, Update saves changes and exits the form
questions.explanation: Insert creates a brand-new record from the current form values, and Update saves changes to the existing record; in both cases the user is returned to the previous list rather than left on the form (B). This contrasts with Save, which commits changes but keeps you on the form, so the options that 'remain on the form' confuse Insert/Update with Save behavior.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Form save, insert, and update

questions.question: How is the Event Log different from the Event Registry?
options: Event Log contains generated Events, the Event Registry is a table of Event definitions
Event Log is formatted in the Log style, the Event Registry displays different fields
Event Log lists Events that were triggered by integrations, the Event Registry lists the Events that were triggered during the day (24-hour period)
Event Log is the same as the Event Registry
questions.explanation: The Event Log (sysevent) records actual event instances that the system has generated and queued, while the Event Registry (sysevent_register) is the catalog of event definitions that can be fired (A). They are therefore not the same record set (D), and the other options misdescribe the distinction as formatting or time-window differences.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Events and the Event Registry

questions.question: What is a dictionary override?
options: A Dictionary Override is an incoming customer update in an Update Set which applies to the same objects as a newer local customer update
A Dictionary Override is the addition, modification, or removal of anything that could have an effect on IT services
A Dictionary Override is a task within a workflow that requests an action before the workflow can continue
A Dictionary Override sets field properties in extended tables
questions.explanation: A Dictionary Override lets you change selected attributes of an inherited field (such as default value, mandatory, or read-only) on a child table without affecting the parent, so it sets field properties in extended tables (D). Option B defines a Change, option C describes an approval/workflow activity, and option A describes an update collision, none of which is a dictionary override.

questions.question: Which group of permissions is used to control application and module access?
questions.explanation: Applications and modules are shown or hidden based on Roles; you assign a required role to the application menu or module, and only users with that role see it (C). Access Control Rules secure data operations on tables and fields, UI Policies control field behavior on forms, and Assignment Rules route records, so none of those governs navigator visibility.

questions.question: What is a record producer?
options: A Record Producer is a type of Catalog Item that is used for Requests, not Services
A Record Producer creates user records
A Record Producer is a type of Catalog Item that provides easy ordering by bundling requests
A Record Producer is a type of a Catalog Item that allows users to create task-based records from the Service Catalog
questions.explanation: A Record Producer is a special catalog item that presents a friendly, catalog-style form and uses it to create a record on a target table, commonly a task-based table such as Incident (D). Bundling related items for easy ordering describes an Order Guide (C), and Record Producers can create records on many tables rather than only user records (B).

questions.question: Create incident, password reset, and report Outage: what do these services in the service catalog have in common?
options: They direct the user to a record producer
They direct the user to a catalog property
They direct the user to a catalog UI policy
They direct the user to a catalog client script
questions.explanation: Create Incident, Password Reset, and Report Outage all create a record on a target table from a catalog-style form, which is exactly what a Record Producer does (A). Catalog properties, catalog UI policies, and catalog client scripts are configuration or behavior components within catalog items rather than the user-facing item these services point to.

questions.question: What is the import set table?
options: A table where data will be placed, post-transformation
A staging area for imported records
A repository for Update Set information
questions.explanation: The Import Set Table is a temporary staging area that holds incoming rows before a Transform Map maps and moves them to the real target table (C). The table where data lands after transformation is the target table (A), so confusing the staging table with the destination is the key distractor here.

questions.question: What is a characteristic of importing data into ServiceNow?
options: An existing Transform Map can be used one time on the same import set
Coalesce fields are used only after running Transform
Any user can manage and set up import sets
An existing Transform Map can be used multiple times on the same import set
questions.explanation: A saved Transform Map is reusable; you can run it repeatedly against the same import set or against new import sets, so it is not limited to a single use (D, contradicting A). Coalesce fields are evaluated during the transform to match records, and managing import sets requires the ap‐ propriate admin/import role rather than being open to any user.

questions.question: What module in the service catalog application does an administrator access to begin creating a new item?
questions.explanation: Administrators create and manage catalog items from the Maintain Items module, which opens the Catalog Item list where new items are defined (B). Maintain Categories manages the categories items are grouped under, and 'Content Items' and 'Items' are not the standard module used to author catalog items.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Create a catalog item

questions.question: Which of the following allows a user to edit field values in a list without opening the form?
questions.explanation: The List Editor lets users edit field values directly in a list by double-clicking a cell, without opening the record's form (C). Form Designer is a tool for building form layouts, and 'Data Editor' and 'Edit Menu' are not the ServiceNow feature that enables inline list editing.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Editing fields from a list

questions.question: Which three variable types can be added to a service catalog item?
options: Number List, Single Line Text, and Reference
Multiple Choice, Select Box, and Checkbox
questions.explanation: Multiple Choice, Select Box, and Checkbox are all valid catalog variable types (D). The other options pair real types with invented ones such as 'Ordered' and 'Number List', which are not standard Service Catalog variable types, making D the only set composed entirely of valid choices.

questions.question: How are workflows moved between instances?
options: Workflows are moved using Update Sets
Workflows are moved using Transform Maps
Workflows are moved using Application Sets
Workflows cannot be moved between instances
questions.explanation: Workflows are configuration records, so they are captured and promoted between instances using Update Sets like other customizations (A). Transform Maps move imported data rather than configuration, 'Application Sets' is not a ServiceNow migration mechanism, and workflows certainly can be moved, ruling out D.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Moving customizations with Update Sets

questions.question: The baseline service catalog homepage contains links to which of the following components?
options: Record Producers, Order Guides, and Catalog Items
Order Guides, Item Variables, and Workflows
Order Guides, Catalog Items, and Workflows
Record Producers, Order Guides, and Item Variables
questions.explanation: The baseline catalog homepage surfaces the user-orderable building blocks: Record Producers, Order Guides, and Catalog Items (A). Item Variables and Workflows are internal configuration and behavior elements that drive items behind the scenes rather than standalone links shown to users on the homepage.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true when a new table is created by extending another table?
options: The new table archives the parent table and assumed its roles in the database
The new table inherits all of the Business Rules, Client Scripts, and UI Policies of the parent table, but none of the existing fields
The new table inherits all of the fields of the parent table and can also contain new fields unique to itself
The new table inherits all of the fields, but does not inherit Access Control rules, Client Scripts, and UI Policies of the parent table
questions.explanation: An extended (child) table inherits all fields from its parent and can also define its own additional fields (C). Inheritance also carries over Business Rules, Client Scripts, UI Policies, and ACLs, so option B (no fields) and option D (no ACLs/scripts) both understate what a child table receives.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Table extension and inheritance

questions.question: Where can admins check which release is running on an ServiceNow instance?
questions.explanation: The Stats module (stats.do) reports instance details including the current build name, build date, and release version (B). The Memory Stats module focuses on JVM memory, there is no 'System.upgraded' table that reports the release, and the Transactions log records request activity rather than version information.

questions.question: A knowledge article must be which of the following states to display to a user?
questions.explanation: An article must be in the Published state before end users can read it in the knowledge base (A). Draft articles are still being authored, Retired articles have been removed from active circulation, and 'Reviewed' is part of the workflow rather than the state that exposes the article to users.

questions.question: What is the name of the conversational bot platform that provides assistance to help users obtain information, make decisions, and perform common tasks?
questions.explanation: Virtual Agent is ServiceNow's conversational bot platform that uses topics and natural language to help users find information, make decisions, and complete common tasks (C). Connect Chat is person-to-person messaging, 'Live Feed' is a social collaboration stream, and 'Answer Agent' is not a ServiceNow product.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a related list?
options: To dot-walk to a core table
questions.explanation: A Related List displays records from another table that are related to the current record, such as the Tasks attached to a Request, presenting related records (D). It visualizes an existing relationship rather than creating one (A), and it shows whole records rather than individual related fields (C).

questions.question: WHICH ONE OF THE FOLLOWING STATEMENTS DESCRIBES THE PURPOSE OF A SERVICE CATALOG WORKFLOW?
options: A Service Catalog workflow generates three basic components: item variable types, tasks, and approvals
Although a Service Catalog workflow cannot send notifications, the workflow drives complex fulfillment processes
A Service Catalog workflow is used to drive complex fulfillment processes and sends notifications to defined users or groups
A Service Catalog workflow generates three basic components: item variable types, tasks, and notifications
questions.explanation: A Service Catalog workflow automates the fulfillment of a request, driving complex processes and sending notifications to the appropriate users or groups (C). Workflows absolutely can send notifications, which makes B false, and they do not 'generate' item variable types, so the lists in A and D mischaracterize what a workflow produces.

questions.question: Which term best describes something that is created, has worked performed upon it, and is eventually moved to a state of closed?
questions.explanation: A Task is the core record type that is opened, worked, and eventually closed; incidents, problems, changes, and catalog tasks all extend the Task table and follow this lifecycle (D). A report visualizes data, a workflow automates a process, and an event is a fleeting system signal, none of which describes a worked-and-closed record.

questions.question: Which are valid ServiceNow user authentication methods? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: ServiceNow can authenticate users against its Local database, against an external directory via LDAP, and through Single Sign-On (SSO) using SAML/OIDC - B, C, and D. 'XML feed' and 'FTP authentication' are data-transfer concepts, not user authentication methods.

questions.question: Access control rules may be defined with which of the following permission requirements? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: An ACL grants access only when its requirements pass, and those requirements are a required Role, a Condition (conditional expression), and an optional Script that returns true/false - A, B, and D. Assignment Rules route work rather than secure data, User Criteria governs catalog and knowledge visibility rather than ACLs, and groups are assigned roles instead of being referenced directly by an ACL.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Access control rule requirements

questions.question: Which one of these applications is available to all users?
questions.explanation: The Self-Service application is designed for every user and requires no special role, giving access to common needs such as the catalog, knowledge, and a user's own requests (D). Change, Incident, and Facilities are role-gated fulfiller applications that only appropriately roled users can see.

questions.question: ServiceNow is a single-instance, multiple tenant architecture?
questions.explanation: ServiceNow uses a multi-instance architecture, where each customer gets their own dedicated application instance and database rather than sharing one multi-tenant instance, so the statement is False (B). This isolation is a core differentiator that allows independent upgrades and customizations per customer.

questions.question: What is the main UI component of the ServiceNow platform?
questions.explanation: The Application Navigator is one of the primary UI components, providing the left-hand menu used to filter and open applications and modules (D). The correct platform terms are the Banner Frame at the top and the Application Navigator on the left, so 'Banner Navigator' and 'Application Frame' mix those names incorrectly.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Navigation and the user interface

questions.question: There are six common types of interfaces. Which interface enables the user to enter data?
options: Homepage: Consists of navigational elements, functional controls, and platform information.
List: Display records from a data table, as well as allow you to edit the record information using the List Editor functionally.
Form: Data is entered into ServiceNow through forms
Dashboard: Enable you to display multiple performance analytics, reporting and other widgets on a single screen.
Maps: Display ServiceNow data graphically on a Google map
Timelines: Used to track tasks or projects
questions.explanation: The interface through which data is commonly entered into ServiceNow by the user.

questions.question: Which type of interface enables you to display multiple performance analytics, reporting and other widgets on a single screen?
questions.explanation: A Dashboard is the interface that assembles multiple widgets - Performance Analytics scorecards, reports, and other content - onto a single screen (C). A Form shows one record, a List shows rows from a table, and a Timeline visualizes scheduled tasks, so none of those aggregate widgets the way a dashboard does.

questions.question: What are the three components of a filter condition?
questions.explanation: Every filter condition in ServiceNow is built from three parts: a Field (the column to evaluate), an Operator (such as 'is', 'contains', '>'), and a Value to compare against - B, C, D. The Table is what you are filtering on, not a component of the individual condition itself.

questions.question: Configuration will not affect what others see on their forms.
questions.explanation: Configuration changes (made via Configure / Form Design) alter the form layout for everyone who uses that view, so the statement is False (B). This is the key distinction from Personalization, which uses the gear icon and changes only the current user's own view.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Form configuration vs. personalization

questions.question: What displays a set of records from a table?
questions.explanation: A List displays a set of records from a table, one record per row (D). A View is a saved arrangement of fields on a form or list rather than the record set itself, and a Dashboard aggregates widgets - neither is the construct that shows multiple table records.

questions.question: A user is stored in which table?
questions.explanation: User records are stored in the User [sys_user] table (A). sys_user_group is the Group table, while syst_user_profile and user_profile are not real platform table names, making the other options invalid.

questions.question: A group is stored in which table?
questions.explanation: Groups are stored in the Group [sys_user_group] table (C). sys_user is the User table, and 'user group' and 'sys_user_group_profile' are not valid platform table names.

questions.question: What are the 6 methods available for user authentication?
options: Local Database: The user name and password in their user record in the instance database.
Multifactor: The user name and password in the database and passcode sent to the user's mobile device that has Google Authenticator installed
LDAP: The user name and password are accessed via LDAP in the corporate directory, which has a matching user account in the database.
SAML 2.0: The user name and password configured in a SAML identity provider account, which has a matching user account in the database.
OAuth 2.0: The user name and password of OAuth identity provider, which has a matching user account in the database.
Digest Token: An encrypted digest of the user name and password in the user record.
questions.explanation: ServiceNow supports six authentication methods, and all six listed are valid: Local Database, Multifactor, LDAP, SAML 2.0, OAuth 2.0, and Digest Token (A - F). Local Database checks credentials stored on the instance, while LDAP/SAML/OAuth delegate to an external identity provider with a matching local user record.

questions.question: A role is recorded in which table?
questions.explanation: Roles in ServiceNow are records in the Role [sys_user_role] table (option D). sys_user is the User table (people, not roles), and sys_user_profile / sys_user_record are not real platform tables. User-to-role assignments live in sys_user_has_role, but the role definitions themselves live in sys_user_role.

questions.question: What are the 5 provided roles by ServiceNow?
options: System Administrator: The admin role provides access to all platform features, applications, functions and data.
Specialized Administrator: Specialized administrator roles manage specific functions or applications, such as Assignment Rules, Knowledge base, reports, or web services
Fulfiller: Users with the ITIL role may fulfill ITIL activities associated with the ITIL workflow, including Incident and Change management.
Approver: Users with the Approver user role can perform all requester actions and may view or modify approval records directed to the approver
Requester: Also known as Employee Self Service (ESS) users, these users have no roles but can submit and manage their own requests, access public pages, etc.
questions.explanation: ServiceNow describes five general user/role categories: System Administrator, Specialized Administrator, Fulfiller (ITIL), Approver, and Requester/ESS - all five options apply (A - E). Note the Requester/ESS 'user' technically holds no assigned role, which is why ESS users can still submit their own requests and view public pages.

questions.question: What are the two aspects to LDAP integration?
questions.explanation: LDAP integration serves two purposes: Data Population - importing user and group records from the directory into ServiceNow - and Authentication, validating login credentials against the LDAP server (A, D). Data formatting and Authorization are handled separately (by transform maps and ACLs/roles), not by the LDAP integration itself.

questions.question: ServiceNow uses what term to describe all the data saved within a particular form?
questions.explanation: All the data captured on a single form is saved as one Record - a row in the underlying table (C). Fields are the individual data elements within that record, the Form is just the visual layout used to view/edit it, and a List shows many records at once.

questions.question: Tables are made up of which of the following?
questions.explanation: A table is a grid composed of records (the rows) and fields (the columns) - A and D. Lists and forms are interface views used to display the data in a table, not the structural building blocks of the table itself.

questions.question: Which application is used to change the number format per table?
questions.explanation: The Number Maintenance application (System Definition > Number Maintenance) controls the auto-numbering prefix, number of digits, and starting value per table (A). The other options are not real applications used for this purpose.

questions.question: Record numbers have to be manually incremented
questions.explanation: Record numbers are generated and incremented automatically by the platform based on the table's number-format configuration, so the statement is False (B). Administrators only set the prefix and digit count in Number Maintenance; they never have to increment numbers by hand.

questions.question: What is the master table that contains a record for each table in the database?
questions.explanation: The Table [sys_db_object] table is the dictionary master table that holds one record for every table defined in the instance (B). The other names are not real platform tables.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Tables and the data dictionary

questions.question: Knowledge articles within a knowledge base are grouped by category.
questions.explanation: Within a knowledge base, articles are organized into Categories (and sub-categories), making the statement True (A). Categories give users a browsable structure for finding related articles within each knowledge base.

questions.question: Each knowledge bases can have unique lifecycle workflows, user criteria, category structures, and management assignments.
questions.explanation: Each knowledge base is configured independently, so it can have its own publish/retire workflow, user criteria for read/write access, category hierarchy, and knowledge managers - the statement is True (A). This per-base flexibility lets an organization run, for example, an IT KB and an HR KB with very different governance.

questions.question: What are the four knowledge workflows available in the ServiceNow base instance?
options: Approval publish: Request approval from a manager of the knowledge base before moving the article it the publish state
Instant Publish: Immediately publishes a draft article without requiring an approval
Instant Retire: Immediately retires a published article without requiring an approval
Retire Knowledge: Moves a knowledge article to the retired state.
questions.explanation: The ServiceNow base instance ships four knowledge workflows: Approval Publish, Instant Publish, Instant Retire, and Retire Knowledge. Options A-D each describe one of these, so all four are correct. New knowledge bases default to the Instant Publish/Retire workflows but can be switched to the approval-based workflows.

questions.question: What is a way that you can mark a knowledge article for review?
questions.explanation: Using 'Flag Article' lets a reader mark an article so its owner/knowledge manager will review it - for example to report an error or outdated content (A). 'Review', 'Bookmark', and 'On Hold' are not the knowledge flagging action.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Flag a knowledge article

questions.question: What are the two pathways to view feedback left on a published article?
options: Knowledge base > my knowledge > flagged articles
questions.explanation: Feedback/flags on published articles can be reached through Knowledge > Articles > My Flagged (articles you flagged) and Knowledge > Articles > Published (open a published article to read its feedback) - A and D match the source answer. The other two navigation paths do not exist in the base Knowledge application.

questions.question: What is the purpose of flagging an article in a knowledge base?
options: To mark an article to read later.
Allow a user to submit feedback about an article
questions.explanation: Flagging an article allows a user to submit feedback about it to the knowledge owner/manager (B). While reporting an error (C) is one reason someone might flag, the broader purpose of the flag feature is the feedback channel itself; flagging is not a personal 'read later' bookmark (A).
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Flag a knowledge article

questions.question: What defines conditions that are evaluated against users to determine which users can create, read, write, and retire knowledge articles.
questions.explanation: User Criteria are reusable records that define which users (by role, group, company, department, etc.) can create, read, write, or retire articles in a knowledge base (C). The other terms are not the ServiceNow mechanism for knowledge access control.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - User criteria for Knowledge

questions.question: Where would you go in ServiceNow to order services and products offered by various departments?
questions.explanation: The Service Catalog is the storefront where users browse and order services and products offered by various departments (A). Self Service is a broader application area that contains the catalog along with knowledge and requests, but the specific place to order items is the Service Catalog itself.

questions.question: What refers to an application or system that accesses a remote service or another computer system, known as a server?
questions.explanation: A Client is the application or system that connects to and consumes services from a remote server (B). In ServiceNow's client-server model, the browser is the client and the instance is the server, which is why client-side scripts run in the browser.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Client vs. server scripting

questions.question: Database live at the data center.
questions.explanation: ServiceNow databases reside in the data center(s) that host the customer's instances, so the statement is True (A). The application and database tiers live in ServiceNow's hosted infrastructure, while the user only needs a browser to reach them.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Tables and the database

questions.question: Business rules are used to enforce mandatory data on a form.
questions.explanation: Business Rules are server-side scripts that run during database operations (insert/update/delete/query); they do not control mandatory fields on a form, so the statement is False (B). Making a field mandatory on a form is the job of a UI Policy (or the dictionary), while Data Policies enforce mandatory data regardless of the entry path.

questions.question: UI policy can make fields read-only, mandatory, or hidden.
questions.explanation: UI Policies dynamically change a field's state on a form - making it read-only, mandatory, or hidden based on conditions - so the statement is True (A). They do this client-side without code, which is the standard no-script way to control field behavior on forms.

questions.question: Which are states that you can make a field on a form using UI policy?
questions.explanation: A UI Policy can set three field states: read-only, mandatory, and hidden (A, D, F). 'Write-only', 'Necessary', and 'Empty' are not valid UI Policy field states.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - UI Policy field states

questions.question: Data Policy can enforce mandatory data on import.
questions.explanation: Data Policies enforce data rules (such as mandatory fields) no matter how the data enters the system - including via Import Sets and web services - so the statement is True (A). This is the key advantage over UI Policies, which only apply when a user interacts with a form.

questions.question: UI action can prompt that an incident has been successfully submitted.
questions.explanation: A UI Action can run script that displays a confirmation message (for example via gs.addInfoMessage) telling the user an incident was submitted, so the statement is True (A). UI Actions add buttons/links that can execute exactly this kind of client- or server-side logic.

questions.question: What is the difference between UI policy and UI action?
options: UI Action can make fields read-only, mandatory, or hidden. while UI Policy can make a save button visible for appropriate users.
UI Policy can make fields read-only, mandatory, or hidden. while UI Action can make a save button visible for appropriate users.
questions.explanation: UI Policies control field states (read-only, mandatory, hidden) on a form, while UI Actions add controls such as buttons/links - for example a save button shown to appropriate users - making B correct. Option A simply swaps the two definitions.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - UI Policies and UI Actions

questions.question: Which one of the following statements describes a characteristic of role assignment?
options: Roles can contain other roles, when you are assigned a role, you inherit all the roles within that role
Users can click on the Personalize Role feature to try different roles
A role is granted to a user by the System Administrator
Each user has a role in the ServiceNow platform
questions.explanation: Roles can contain other roles, and being granted a parent role automatically grants all the child roles it contains (A). There is no 'Personalize Role' feature (B), roles are commonly delivered via groups rather than only by an admin one-by-one (C), and ESS users can have no role at all, so not every user has a role (D).
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Roles and role inheritance

questions.question: What are best practices regarding users/groups/roles? (Choose two.)
options: You should never assign roles to groups.
You should assign roles to users.
You should assign roles to groups
You should add users to groups
questions.explanation: ServiceNow best practice is to assign roles to groups and add users to those groups (C, D), so access is managed by group membership rather than per-user. Assigning roles directly to individual users (B) is discouraged because it is hard to maintain, and 'never assign roles to groups' (A) is the opposite of the recommendation.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Roles and groups best practice

questions.question: Which configuration allows you to use a script to coalesce data in import sets?
questions.explanation: Conditional coalesce lets you write a script to determine the match condition during a transform, rather than relying on one or more fixed coalesce fields (C). Single-field and multiple-field coalesce match on declared fields without scripting, and 'No coalesce' always inserts new records.

questions.question: Which one of the following modules can be used to view field settings for a table?
questions.explanation: The Tables & Columns module (System Definition) lets you select a table and inspect its columns/field settings (A). 'Columns and Fields' and 'Tables and Fields' are not real modules, and Access Control is for ACLs, not field definitions.

questions.question: What is a role in ServiceNow?
options: A role is one record m the Role [sys_user_role] table
A role is one record in the Role Iuser_sys_role] table
A role is a persona used In Live Feed Chat
A role Is a set of modules for a particular application
questions.explanation: A role is a single record in the Role [sys_user_role] table that bundles a set of permissions which can be granted to users and groups (A). 'user_sys_role' is not a real table, a role is not a chat persona, and a role is not simply a set of application modules.

questions.question: What are the three components of a filter condition?
questions.explanation: A filter condition is composed of a Field, an Operator, and a Value (A) - for example 'Priority' 'is' '1'. The other options substitute 'Condition' or 'Variable' for one of the three true components.

questions.question: Which one of the following statements is true?
options: When an incident form is saved, all the Work Notes field text is recorded to the Activity Log field
When an incident form is saved, the Work Notes field text is overwritten each time work is logged against the incident
When an incident form is saved, the impact field is calculated by adding the Prion:, and Urgency values
When an Incident form is saved, the Additional Comments field text is cleared and recorded to the Work Notes section
questions.explanation: Work Notes and Additional Comments are journal fields stored in sys_journal_field; on save the typed text is cleared from the input and appended to the activity log/stream as a timestamped entry, so option A is correct. Journal fields append rather than overwrite (B is wrong), Impact/Urgency derive Priority rather than Impact (C is wrong), and Additional Comments post as their own entries, not into the Work Notes section (D is wrong).
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Journal fields (Work notes / Additional comments)

questions.question: What kind of data can import sets use to populate tables in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: Import Sets can load data from file-based sources such as XML, CSV, and Excel (B). The options containing CSS are wrong (CSS is a stylesheet language, not a data format), and SOAP/REST are web-service transport mechanisms rather than the import file types this question targets.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Import data using Import Sets

questions.question: What ServiceNow tables can administrators define as "destinations" for imported data, when using transform maps in the system import sets application?
options: The Task table is the only table that can be a destination for imported data in the Transform Map module
The Incident. Problem. Change, Task, and Service Catalog tables are the only tables that can be a destination for imported data m the Transform Map module
Only the Incident Problem, and Change tables can be a destination for imported data in the Transform Map module
Any ServiceNow table can be a destination for imported data in the Transform Map module
questions.explanation: When using a Transform Map in System Import Sets, an administrator can map the import-set staging fields onto the columns of any ServiceNow table they choose, so the destination can be ANY table (option D). There is no built-in limit to Incident, Problem, Change, Task, or Service Catalog tables.

questions.question: Which one of the following is not a type of visual task board?
questions.explanation: The three Visual Task Board types are Freeform, Guided, and Flexible; 'Feature' is not a board type, so it is the correct NOT answer (A). Freeform boards stand alone, while Guided and Flexible boards are backed by records on a table.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Visual Task Board structure

questions.question: What is the purpose of a data policy?
options: Data Policies standardize data in Update Sets
Data Policies apply to lists to standard data
questions.explanation: Data Policies enforce data consistency by applying field rules (such as mandatory or read-only) regardless of how the data enters the system - form, import, or web service (C). They are not security/ACL controls (A), have nothing to do with Update Sets (B), and are not list-only (D).

questions.question: A change request has been approved and assigned to you as the system administrator to change the incident number prefix from the default of "INC" to the company standard "IN" what are the next steps to be taken
options: Go to the Number Maintenance application and change the prefix to "IN" for incident
Create a Business Rule that modifies the prefix before the Insert operation
The prefix of an incident cannot be changed because it is a built-in feature
Submit a Change Request to ServiceNow Technical Support
questions.explanation: Number prefixes are configurable per table in the Number Maintenance application, so you simply change the Incident prefix there to 'IN' (A). A custom Business Rule (B) is unnecessary complexity, the prefix is not locked (C), and ServiceNow Support does not need to be involved (D).

questions.question: How do you make a list filter available to everyone?
options: Make active, set visibility, and save
Assign a name, set visibility, and save
Assign a group, set visibility, and save
Make active, assign a name, and save
questions.explanation: To share a filter as a saved Filter, you give it a name, set its Visible to / visibility to Everyone, and save it (B). A name is required to store the filter, and the visibility setting (not a 'group' or an 'active' flag) is what makes it available to all users.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Save and share a filter

questions.question: What is not an example of a UI action?
questions.explanation: UI Actions render as form buttons, list buttons, context menu items, and related links, so options B (form buttons), C (list buttons), and D (related links) are all UI Actions. Search is built-in navigation/list filtering, not a UI Action, making A the correct 'NOT a UI Action' answer.

questions.question: In addition to the admin role, which one of the following roles allows a user to add or remove fields from a list?
questions.explanation: The personalize_control role lets a non-admin user personalize lists by adding or removing columns (A). The other listed role names are not the role that grants list-personalization rights.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Event Registry?
options: The Event Registry lists all Events that have successfully completed within a 24-hour period
The Event Registry is a list of all Events that originate through an integration
The Event Registry is a module that provides Event definitions
The Event Registry is a list of all Events that have successfully completed after being Invoked by a script
questions.explanation: The Event Registry (sysevent_register) is the module that holds Event definitions - it documents which events exist in the platform and what fires them (option C). It is not a rolling list of recently completed events; that is the Event Log (sysevent), which records actual event instances.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the fitter navigator in the application navigator?
options: Filter applications in order of use
Quickly navigate to applications and modules
List applications In order of Top Requests
questions.explanation: The filter navigator (the type-ahead box at the top of the Application Navigator) lets you quickly find and jump to any application or module by typing part of its name (option B). Expanding or collapsing application menus is a side effect of browsing the navigator, not the purpose of the filter.

questions.question: What is the difference between a Ul policy and data policy?
options: Data Policies run only after Ul Policies run successfully
Data Policies run regardless of how data is entered Into ServiceNow, while Ul Policies are used for form interactions
Data Policies can be converted into Ul Policies, but Ul Policies can not be converted into Data Policies
Data Policies run when data is entered through the form, by an Import Set or by web services, while Ul Policies are set only by web services
questions.explanation: Data Policies enforce mandatory/read-only rules no matter how a record is created or updated - form, Import Set, or web service - whereas UI Policies act only on the form/client interaction (option B). Option D is wrong because UI Policies govern forms, not 'only web services.' A Data Policy can also be converted to a UI Policy, but that is not the defining difference.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Data Policies vs UI Policies

questions.question: What is an event in ServiceNow?
options: An Event is a trigger that has a direct response in the platform
An Event is an indication to the ServiceNow processes that something has occurred
An Event is an indicator that a Priority 1 (P1) Incident has been logged
An Event is a recognized, scheduled occurrence of a process
questions.explanation: An Event is a record/indication, written to the event queue, signaling that something noteworthy has happened in the platform (B). It is not itself a direct trigger/response (A), is not limited to P1 incidents (C), and is not a scheduled job (D).

questions.question: Which one of the following is an accurate list of changes that are captured in an update set?
options: Changes made to tables, forms, schedules, and client scripts
Changes made to tables, forms, views, and fields
Changes made to: tables, forms. Business Rules, and data records
Changes made to: tables. forms groups, and configuration items (Cls)
questions.explanation: Update Sets capture configuration/customization changes such as tables, forms, schedules, and client scripts (A). The options that include data records, groups, or configuration items are wrong because Update Sets move customizations, not data records or CMDB CIs.

questions.question: What are the three permission requirements that must evaluate to true for an access control rule to apply? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: An Access Control rule grants access only when all three of its permission requirements pass: the required Roles, the Conditions, and the Script must each evaluate to true (any empty one is treated as true). Mapping to the options, these are Conditions (A), Roles (C), and Script (D); the 'table.' variants are corrupted text, not requirements.

questions.question: When does the submit button appear on a form?
options: When changing the reference field in an existing record
questions.explanation: The Submit button appears when you are creating a brand-new record that has not yet been saved (B). Once a record exists, the form shows Update/Save instead, so the options about editing existing records do not apply.

questions.question: New records, new groups, and modified configuration items (Cls): what do they have in common?
options: They are included in an Update Set
They are not captured in an Update Set
They do not have anything in common
questions.explanation: Data records, group records, and CMDB configuration items are data - not configuration - so by default they are NOT captured in an Update Set (B). Update Sets track customizations like business rules, UI policies, and tables, which is exactly why data records must be moved separately.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - What Update Sets capture

questions.question: When using the performance analytics application in the Now platform, what kind of KPI signals are used to make decisions that statistically support long term workflow stability?
questions.explanation: In Performance Analytics, KPI Signals surface meaningful changes, and Anti-signals are the configured signal type used to filter out noise so decisions are based on statistically stable, longterm trends (C). The source records C; 'Long-term', 'Non-', and 'Stability' signals are not the named signal types.

questions.question: Which fields can be configured in reporting to perform arithmetic, coalesce, concatenation, and length?
questions.explanation: Function fields let you build calculated values in reports - arithmetic, coalesce, concatenation, length, and more - without changing the underlying table (B). 'Sourcing', 'Computational', and 'Calculation' fields are not the ServiceNow reporting feature for this.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Function fields in reports

questions.question: The ServiceNow Virtual agent provides assistance within a messaging interface. Which capability allows end users to configure Virtual agent to intercept and help resolve submitted incidents?
questions.explanation: Incident Auto-Resolution is the Virtual Agent capability that intercepts submitted incidents and attempts to deflect/resolve them through conversational topics and recommended solutions (A). The other option names are not real ServiceNow capabilities.

questions.question: Which plugin allows users to Install multiple applications, application-customizations. Or plugins at once?
options: Application Integration and Plugin Delivery (A1PD) SpokeBatch Install
Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery (CICD) SpokeBatch Install
Multiple Integration and Process Delivery (MIPD) SpokeBatch Install
Quick Integration and Multiple Delivery (QIMD) SpokeBatch Install
questions.explanation: The source marks B (CICD) as correct, tying batch installation to the Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery capability that can apply applications, customizations, and plugins together in one operation. The other three acronyms (A1PD, MIPD, QIMD) are invented and do not correspond to any ServiceNow plugin.

questions.question: How can administrators utilize the same content for different notification channels?
questions.explanation: Common notification content lets administrators author a message body once and reuse it across multiple delivery channels (such as email and push), avoiding duplicate maintenance (C). The other choices describe defaults, actionable buttons, or 'related' content, none of which is the mechanism for sharing one body across channels.

questions.question: Which certificate-based authentication methods can be enabled so that users can log into the service portal? (Select all that apply) select 2 answers from the below options
questions.explanation: ServiceNow supports certificate-based login using government-issued smart cards: the Common Access Card (CAC) and the Personal Identity Verification (PIV) card - C and E. EVA, OVC, and DAC are fabricated acronyms and are not certificate authentication methods in the platform.

questions.question: Which plugin needs to be activated in order to translate the content of a catalog item to multiple languages?
questions.explanation: The Localization Framework plugin (com.glide.localization_framework) provides the tooling to translate platform content, including catalog item fields, into multiple languages (A). The other plugin names and identifiers are not real - there is no 'Translation Framework', 'Multiple Language Framework', or 'Language AI Framework' plugin of this kind.

questions.question: Where in Flow Designer can users access information about actions that are added to the flow?
questions.explanation: Flow Designer includes a Help Panel that displays contextual information and documentation about the actions you add to a flow (C). 'Virtual Agent Help', 'Local Action Help', and 'Flow Assistant' are not Flow Designer interface elements, so they are incorrect.

questions.question: How are local flow variables accessed in the Flow Designer Data panel?
questions.explanation: In Flow Designer, outputs and variables surface in the Data panel as data pills, which you drag into later steps to pass values along (D). Flow Designer does not expose local variables as 'scratchpad variables', 'tabs', or 'icons' - those terms describe other tools, making them distractors.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Data pills in Flow Designer

questions.question: Which section of the ServiceNow UI allows you to perform a global search?
questions.explanation: Global (text) search is performed from the search icon in the banner frame - the bar across the top of every page (B). The Application Navigator filters the menu, not global records; the list pane and content frame display results and forms but do not host the global search control.

questions.question: What would not appear in the application navigator if 'service' is typed into the filter field?
questions.explanation: The Application Navigator filter matches the text you type anywhere in an application or module label. 'Business Services', 'Self-Service', and 'Service Portal' all contain the string 'service', so they remain visible, while 'Incident > Assigned to me' contains no match and is filtered out (D).

questions.question: Which of the following is used to categorize, flag, and locate records?
questions.explanation: Tags let users label records with keywords so they can be categorized, flagged for attention, and quickly located later (C). Search only finds records, Favorites bookmark navigator modules rather than individual records, and Bookmarks are a browser-level concept - none provides the categorize/flag/locate combination.

questions.question: Which tool should be used to populate commonly used fields in a form?
questions.explanation: A Template stores a set of preset field values that can be applied to a new record, quickly populating the fields you fill in repeatedly (A). A Reference Qualifier filters reference-field choices, a Formatter adds non-field UI elements to a form, and an Assignment Rule routes records to groups/users - none of which pre-fills common fields.

questions.question: How is a group defined in ServiceNow?
options: A group is one record stored in the Group Type [sys_user_group_type] table
A group is one record stored in the Group [sys_user_group] table
A group defines a set of users that share the same location
A group defines a set of users that share the same job title
questions.explanation: A group is a single record in the Group [sys_user_group] table; users are linked to it through group-membership records (B). A group is defined by a shared purpose (for example, an assignment or notification target), not by users happening to share a location (C) or job title (D), and sys_user_group_type is a separate lookup table, not where the group record lives (A).

questions.question: What is a notification?
options: A new Knowledge article created by a Business Rule
A tool for alerting users that events that concern them have occurred
A message through Connect related to a Change Request
questions.explanation: A Notification is the platform mechanism for alerting users that an event affecting them has occurred - for example, emailing the assignee when a record is updated (B). It is not a Knowledge article, a Connect chat message, or a file attachment, so the other options mischaracterize the feature.

questions.question: What are two ways to generate an Event? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Events are written to the event queue by server-side logic. A Business Rule can call gs.event‐ Queue() to fire an event, and a Workflow can include an activity that generates one - A and B. Creating a log entry or publishing a Knowledge article does not, by itself, register an event in the queue.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Events and the event registry

questions.question: Which core table in the ServiceNow platform provides a series of standard fields used on each of the tables that extend it, such as the Incident [incident] and Problem [problem] tables?
questions.explanation: The Task [task] table is the base table from which Incident, Problem, Change, and other process tables extend, so they all inherit common fields like Number, State, Priority, and Assigned to (A). 'Assignment', 'Service', and 'Workflow' are not the parent table for these records.

questions.question: Which of the following statements describes how data is organized in a table?
options: A column is a field in the database and a record is one user
A column is one field and a record is one row
A column is one field and a record is one column
A column contains data from one user and a record is one set of fields
questions.explanation: In a ServiceNow table, each column corresponds to a single field (attribute), and each record is a single row spanning all of those columns (B). Option A wrongly ties records to 'one user', C confuses a record with a column, and D mislabels columns as user-specific - only B states the column/field and record/row relationship correctly.

questions.question: What is a sys_id?
options: Unique 32-character identifier that is assigned to every record
Unique 64-character identifier that is assigned to every record
questions.explanation: A sys_id is a globally unique 32-character (hexadecimal GUID) identifier the platform assigns to every record in every table (A). It is 32 characters, not 64 (ruling out D), and it is an identifier rather than any kind of Business Rule (ruling out B and C).

questions.question: When creating a global custom table named 'abc', what is the table name that is automatically assigned by the platform?
questions.explanation: When you create a custom table in the global application scope, ServiceNow automatically prefixes the internal name with u_, producing u_abc (C). The sys_ prefix is reserved for core platform tables, snc_ is a ServiceNow-internal namespace, and an unprefixed 'abc' is not how global custom tables are named.

questions.question: Access control rules may provide access security for which of the following database objects?
options: For a specific role, group, or user
For a specific row, column, or table
For a specific CMDB Configuration item
questions.explanation: Access Control rules (ACLs) provide security for specific rows, columns (fields), and tables. An ACL is named in the form table.field and evaluates roles, conditions, and scripts. Securing an individual CMDB CI is not how ACLs are scoped, so option B is correct.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Contextual security: ACL rules

questions.question: What is the primary application used to load data into ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: System Import Sets is the application used to bring external data into ServiceNow: you load rows into a staging table, then transform them onto a target table (C). System Update Sets moves configuration between instances rather than loading data, and the other two are unrelated to importing.

questions.question: Which of the following steps can be used to import new data into ServiceNow from a spreadsheet?
options: Load Data, Create Transform Map, Run Transform
Define Data Source, Select Transform Map, Run Transform
Select Import Set, Select Transform Map, Run Transform
questions.explanation: To import new spreadsheet data you Load Data (which creates the import set staging table), then Create a Transform Map to align source columns to target fields, then Run Transform to write the records to the target table. Option B captures this end-to-end flow for new data.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Load data using import sets

questions.question: Which tool is used for creating dependencies between configuration items in the CMDB?
questions.explanation: The CI Relationship Editor lets you create, modify, and delete relationships between specific CIs, defining the parent CI, the child/target CI, and the relationship verb (e.g., 'Runs on'). The CI Class Manager, by contrast, administers the class tree and class-level settings, so option A is the correct tool.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - CI Class Manager / CMDB

questions.question: What is the difference between a UI policy and data policy?
options: Data Policies run when data is entered through the form, by an Import Set, or by web services, while UI Policies are set only by web services
