Data Policies can be converted into UI Policies, but UI Policies cannot be converted into Data Policies
Data Policies run regardless of how data is entered into ServiceNow, while UI Policies are used for form interactions
Data Policies run only after UI Policies run successfully
questions.explanation: Data Policies enforce field rules at the data layer, so they apply no matter how the data arrives - form, import set, web service, or script - whereas UI Policies act only on the form in the browser (C). A is wrong because UI Policies are not 'web services only', and D invents an execution-order dependency that does not exist.

questions.question: What are the steps to Retrieve an update set?
options: Verify Update Set is Complete, Retrieve, Preview, Apply
Verify Update Set is Complete, Test Connection, Apply
Verify Update Set is Complete, Test Connection, Commit
Verify Update Set is Complete, Retrieve, Preview, Commit
questions.explanation: On the target instance you confirm the update set is Complete on the source, Retrieve it across the instance connection, Preview it to catch collisions, and then Commit it to apply the changes - option D. 'Apply' is not the final action label (ruling out A), and 'Test Connection' is a setup step, not part of retrieving/committing (ruling out B and C).
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Retrieve and commit update sets

questions.question: Integrationhub enables execution of third-party APIs as a part of a flow. These integrations are referred to as
questions.explanation: In IntegrationHub, related integration actions for a given third-party system are packaged together as a spoke (for example, a Slack or Microsoft Teams spoke) (B). An individual action is one step inside a spoke, and a connection stores credentials/endpoints - neither term names the packaged integration itself.

questions.question: Which of the following protects applications by identifying and restricting access to available files and data?
questions.explanation: Access Control Rules (ACLs) protect applications by checking the roles, conditions, and scripts required before a user can read, write, create, or delete records and fields. This is what restricts access to available files and data, making option C correct.

questions.question: ServiceNow contains a resource which provides the following: a standard and shared set of service related definitions across ServiceNow products and platform that will enable and support true service level reporting. A CMDB framework across our products and platform that will enable and support multiple configuration strategies. What resource do these statements describe?
questions.explanation: The Common Service Data Model (CSDM) is the standard, shared set of service-related table definitions and CMDB framework that ServiceNow products use to enable consistent, true service-level reporting (A). ITSM is a product suite, the CMDB is the database itself, and ITIL is an external best-practice framework - none is the prescriptive data model being described.
questions.reference: ServiceNow - Common Service Data Model solution brief

questions.question: An it manager is responsible for the network and hardware assignment groups, each containing five team members. The members are working on many tasks, but the manager cannot see any tasks on the service desk > my groups work list - even with the filter set to assignment group is network or hardware. What could explain this?
options: The Service Desk > My Groups Work list shows active work tasks that are not yet assigned.
The manager does not have the itil role.
The manager is not a member of the Service Desk group.
The manager is not a member of the Network and Hardware groups.
The Assignment Group manager field is empty.
questions.explanation: 'Service Desk > My Groups Work' shows work for the groups the logged-in user belongs to. The shown filter already targets the Network and Hardware assignment groups, so the manager must be a member of those groups to see their tasks. Not being a member of the Network and Hardware groups (D) is the root cause.

questions.question: What do you need to do before you can use an application-based trigger in your flow?
options: Activate application spoke, and plug-ins as needed
Assign Application trigger role [sn_app_trigger_write] to SME
questions.explanation: Before an application-based trigger is available in a flow, you must activate that application's spoke (and any plugins it depends on) so the trigger and its actions are installed. Once the spoke is active, the trigger appears for selection in Flow Designer, making option C correct.

questions.question: The ServiceNow platform includes which types of interfaces? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: ServiceNow delivers its functionality through Now Mobile Apps, Service Portals, and the Now Platform user interfaces (such as the standard UI and workspaces) - A, D, and E. 'Agent Control Center', 'Back Office Dashboard', and 'Field Service Taskboard' are not standard platform interface categories.

questions.question: Which of the following are not included in an update set, by default? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: Update sets capture customizations, not transactional data. Data records (B), Schedules (E), Database/dictionary data changes (F), and Scheduled Jobs (I) are not included by default because they are considered data rather than tracked customizations. Items like home pages can be added manually but, in this option set, the keyed four are B, E, F, and I.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Data not captured by update sets

questions.question: You are showing your customer a new form that you have created for their new application. They would like to add a field to the form. Where could you do that? (Choose two.)
options: Right click on form header, select Configure > Form Layout
Click on context menu, select Configure > Form Designer
questions.explanation: You can add a field to a form using Form Layout (the slushbucket reached from Configure > Form Layout) or the drag-and-drop Form Designer, both opened from the form's context menu - B and C. 'Fields and Columns module' and 'Field Class Manager module' are not the tools used to place a field on a form.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Form Designer and Form Layout

questions.question: Which ServiceNow resource is a framework that ensures the data your ServiceNow application requires maps correctly to the appropriate CMDB tables?
questions.explanation: The Common Service Data Model (CSDM) is the prescriptive framework that defines where data should live so applications map correctly to the appropriate CMDB tables and classes (A). The other acronyms - SMU, SSM, CMDBCM, CICM - are either fabricated or are tools rather than the data-modeling framework being described.

questions.question: What do you activate when you want to add applications or functionality within your development instance?
questions.explanation: Plugins are the packaged components you activate to add applications, features, or demo data to an instance (D). 'App Package', 'Updated Pack', 'Patch', and 'App Updated Set' are not the mechanism for adding optional functionality - a patch updates platform code rather than adding a feature you choose to enable.

questions.question: What field contains a record's 32-character, unique identifier?
questions.explanation: The sys_id field holds the 32-character globally unique identifier that the platform assigns to every record (D). All the other field names listed - rec_id, u_id, sn_gu_id, and so on - are invented and do not exist as the record's unique identifier.

questions.question: Your company is giving all first line workers a special t-shirt as a recognition for their hard work. Management team wants a way for employees to order the t-shirt, with the ability to specify the preferred size and color. How would you ensure that only first line workers (Non-managers) can submit the order?
options: Create Record Producer and use the Available For list to specify First Line [sn_first_line] role
Create Catalog Item and use the Not Available list to specify the Manager Group
Create Catalog Item and use the Available For list to specify ITIL [itil] role
Create Order Guide and use the User Criteria list to specify First Line [sn_first_line] role
questions.explanation: The source keys this to B - a Catalog Item with size/color variables, using the 'Not Available for' user criteria to exclude the Manager group so only non-managers can order. Note that user criteria typically express who CAN see an item, so an 'Available for: First Line role' approach (option A/D pattern) is the more common positive design; this question tests the exclusion (Not Available) approach.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Apply user criteria to a catalog item

questions.question: What is used frequently to move customizations from one instance to another?
questions.explanation: Update Sets are the standard, frequently used mechanism for capturing configuration changes and moving them between instances (A). The other options - Code Sets, Update Packs, Configuration Logs, Remote/Local Sets, Code Packs - are not real ServiceNow migration features.

questions.question: What icon do you use to change the label on a favorite?
questions.explanation: To rename (relabel) a favorite, you click the Pencil/edit icon next to it, which opens the favorite for editing (C). The Star toggles whether something is a favorite, the Clock shows history, and the other icons do not edit a favorite's label.

questions.question: What needs to be specified, when creating a business rule? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: When creating a Business Rule you select the Table it runs on, the Timing/When (Before, After, Async, or Display) plus the database operations, the Condition that must evaluate true, and the Script to execute. Those four are Table, Timing, Condition, and Script (B, E, H, I).

questions.question: What feature can track the amount of time that a task has been open, to ensure that tasks are completed within an allotted time?
questions.explanation: Service Level Agreements (SLAs) track elapsed time against a target so you can ensure tasks are completed within an allotted period, escalating as deadlines approach (B). An Inactivity Monitor only watches for records sitting untouched, and the 'Task Escalation Clock' and 'Response Time Clock' are not standard ServiceNow features.

questions.question: What is a quick way to create a report from a list view?
options: Click on filter breadcrumb, drag and drop on the Report > Create New module
Click Funnel, define filter conditions, click Create Report
Click Context Menu, select Create Report
Apply filter, right click on column header, select Bar Chart
Apply filter, right click on column header, select Create Report
questions.explanation: From a list view you can apply a filter, right-click the column header you want to group by, and choose Bar Chart (or Pie Chart). ServiceNow immediately generates a report grouped on that column, which you can then refine. This makes option D the quick list-to-report method.

questions.question: What import utility do you use when the field names on the import set match the name of the fields on the target table?
questions.explanation: When source and target field names match, Auto Map Matching Fields (Automatic Mapping) creates the transform-map field mappings for you automatically (B). Mapping Assist is the manual point-and-click mapper for fields that do not match, and 'Schema Mapping'/'Mapping Dashboard' are not the auto-match utility.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Field maps and auto mapping

questions.question: As an it employee what interface would you use, if you wanted to browse internal it documentation, like troubleshooting scripts and faqs?
questions.explanation: The Knowledge (Knowledge Base) application is where ServiceNow stores and lets employees browse internal documentation such as troubleshooting steps and FAQs (A). 'Knowledge Now' and 'ServiceNow Wiki' are not current platform features, and SharePoint and Stack Overflow are external, non-ServiceNow tools.

questions.question: A new service desk employee in latin America complains that the create dates and times are incorrect on their incident list. What would you suggest to fix this issue?
options: Have them use the gear icon to set the employee's time zone.
Recommend they use Chrome, instead of Explorer.
Use the system properties to correct the instance's time zone.
Have them correct the time zone on their computer.
questions.explanation: Incident create dates and times are rendered in each user's configured time zone. The fix is to set the employee's time zone in their ServiceNow user settings via the gear/settings icon (option B), not to change the time zone on their computer.

questions.question: What are three security modules often used by the system administrator? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Administrators commonly use System Properties > Security (security-related system properties), System Security > Access Control (ACL) to manage ACL rules, and System Security > High Security Settings to configure the elevated-privilege/security-admin controls - A, E, and G. The other modules listed either do not exist by those names or are end-user, not admin security, features.

questions.question: When testing a catalog item, having a manager approval flows, which of these best practices would you follow? (Choose three.)
options: Make sure the latest flows are activated.
Use the instance Incognito setting to quickly toggle between requester and approver.
Impersonate the requester to ensure the form works.
Make sure the requester's user record has a manager specified.
Create and select your Testing Update Set, before starting the test cases.
Use your Admin account, so you can approve the items quickly.
questions.explanation: To validly test a catalog item with manager approval you activate the latest flow version (A), impersonate the requester so you experience the form as the end user (C), and confirm the requester has a manager set so the approval routes correctly (D). Approving with your own admin account would bypass realistic approval testing.

questions.question: What is a no-code approach to control the mandatory or read-only state of a form field?
questions.explanation: A UI Policy lets you make a field mandatory, read-only, or hidden using simple conditions, with no scripting required (E). Client Scripts and UI Scripts require JavaScript (so they are not 'nocode'), 'UI Rule' is not a real type, and a UI Action creates buttons rather than controlling field state.

questions.question: When moving multiple update sets at one time, what might you do to facilitate the move?
questions.explanation: Batching update sets lets you group several related update sets under a base set so they are retrieved, previewed, and committed together in the correct order (A). Verify, Test, and Preview are individual steps in the transfer process, not the feature that moves multiple sets at once.

questions.question: What is specified in an access control rule?
options: Table Schema, CRUD, and User Authentication
Object and Operation being secured; Permissions required to access the object
questions.explanation: An ACL rule defines the object and operation being secured (for example, the incident table's read or write) plus the permissions - roles, conditions, and scripts - required to pass it (C). The other options list unrelated concepts; security_admin (D) is the elevated role used to edit ACLs, not what an ACL itself specifies.

questions.question: In the application navigator (The left-hand menu), which icon do you double-click to expand and collapse the list of all applications and modules at once?
questions.explanation: The source keys this to C (Application). In the All/Application Navigator, double-clicking an application header collapses or expands all of its modules at once. The Star shows favorites, the Clock shows history, and the Funnel filters the navigator - none of which expand/collapse every application's modules.

questions.question: What do you call any component that needs to be managed in order to deliver services?
questions.explanation: A Configuration Item (CI) is any component - hardware, software, service, or other asset - that must be managed to deliver IT services, and CIs are stored in the CMDB (C). The CMDB is the database that holds CIs (not the component itself), and Service Offerings and 'CSDM Items' describe other concepts.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Configuration items and the CMDB

questions.question: A new service catalog item is being developed, but should only be visible to managers inside the HR department. What method would you use to fulfill this requirement?
options: Specify the Dept_Mgr role on the catalog content block
Add the Department Manager group to the catalog item's user criteria
Add the Department Manager group to the catalog item's ACL
Only publish the item in the HR service catalog
Use a Dept_Mgr ACL on the HR service catalog
questions.explanation: User Criteria is the supported mechanism for controlling who can see and order Service Catalog items and categories; you build a User Criteria record (by group, role, department, location, etc.) and apply it to the item's Available For / Not Available For lists. Adding the Department Manager group to the item's user criteria (B) cleanly restricts visibility to those managers. ACLs (C, E) secure table records rather than catalog visibility, and simply publishing to a catalog (D) does not limit which users see the item within it.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - User criteria for catalog items

questions.question: A user wants to create a set of filter conditions, where they want to show records which satisfy two conditions: Incidents where the State is Closed, Incidents where Assignment Group is Network after clicking the Funnel icon, what should the user do?
options: Define the first condition; click AND button; define second condition; click Run
Define the first condition; click AND button; define second condition; press enter
Define the first condition; click OR button; define second condition; press enter
Define the first condition; click > icon on breadcrumb, define second condition; click Run
Define the first condition; click > icon on breadcrumb, define second condition; press enter
questions.explanation: When both conditions must be true at the same time, you build them in the condition builder joined by AND, then click Run to apply the filter and return the matching records (A). The OR button (C) would return records meeting either condition, which is not what is asked, and pressing Enter inside a condition row is not the reliable way to execute a multi-condition filter - Run is the explicit action that applies it.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Filters and the condition builder

questions.question: Access control rules are applied to a specific table, like the incident table. What is the object name for a rule that is specific to the incident table and the major incident field?
questions.explanation: An ACL that targets a single field uses the table.field naming convention with the lowercase database names, giving incident.major_incident (E). The names must match the platform field names exactly, so capitalized forms like Incident.Major_Incident (A) are wrong, and the arrow/pipe separators in the other options are not valid ACL object syntax.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Access control rule types

questions.question: Two departments (HR onboarding and Facilities) have come to you, asking for a way for employees to request event Room set up services. The requirements are the same for the form and the task routing to the facilities' assignment group. For HR, the item will be used primarily for the onboarding coordinators, for employee orientation sessions. For Facilities, the item will be used for anyone in the company who needs Room set up services. However, both departments have their own service catalogs. What do you do, to support these requirements?
options: Create one Catalog Item for HR Event Room Set Up and one for Facilities Event Room Set Up; then publish each to the appropriate Catalog.
Create one Catalog Item for Event Room Set Up; then publish to both Catalogs.
Create one Catalog Item for Event Room Set Up; then publish to the Parent Catalog, which is accessible to both HR and Facilities.
Create one Catalog Item for Event Room Set Up; then use ACLs to control access.
questions.explanation: Because a catalog item's Catalogs field accepts multiple catalogs, you build one 'Event Room Set Up' item with the shared form and Facilities task routing, then publish it to both the HR and Facilities catalogs. This reuses one item across catalogs without duplication, making option B correct.

questions.question: After finishing your work on high security settings, what do you do to return to normal admin security levels?
options: Use System Administration > Normal Security module
questions.explanation: Working on High Security Settings requires elevating to the security_admin role, and that elevation lasts only for the current session. Logging out and back in (B) drops the elevated privileges and returns you to your normal admin level. There is no 'Normal Security' module or 'Normal role' to select (A, C), and ending impersonation (E) is unrelated to role elevation.

questions.question: What type of field allows you to look up values from one other table?
questions.explanation: A Reference field stores a pointer (sys_id) to a record in another table, letting a form look up and display values from that related table - for example, the Caller field on Incident referencing sys_user (A). Dot-walking (E) is the technique of traversing through a reference to reach the referenced table's fields, not the field type itself, and the other options are not real ServiceNow field types.

questions.question: Which module would you use to create a new automation of business logic such as approvals, tasks, and notifications?
questions.explanation: Flow Designer, opened from Process Automation > Flow Designer, is the modern no-code/lowcode tool for building automation such as approvals, tasks, and notifications (A). The other module paths listed do not exist as the entry point for creating flows - Flow Administration, Workflow Editor, Process Flow, and Active Flows are not how you launch the Flow Designer builder.

questions.question: Which module is used as the first step for importing data?
questions.explanation: The import process begins with Load Data, which reads the source file or data source into a staging import set table (D). Only after the data is loaded do you map and Transform it into the target table; coalescing is an option configured within the transform map, not a separate first step.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Importing data using import sets

questions.question: When you need to orchestrate business processes across services with little technical user knowledge, which utility would you use?
questions.explanation: Flow Designer provides a no-code, flowchart-style interface that lets admins and citizen developers orchestrate end-to-end processes and integrations without scripting. Since 'Flow Editor' is not an actual ServiceNow tool, the correct answer is Flow Designer (B).

questions.question: When a user reports that they are not able to see modules on the application navigator, what can you do, to see what modules are visible to them?
options: Look up their password, so you can login with their account
questions.explanation: Impersonating the user (D) lets an admin temporarily view the platform exactly as that user sees it - including which application menus and modules their roles expose - without knowing their password. Looking up a password (A) is impossible and a security violation since passwords are hashed, and the chat options do nothing to reveal another user's navigator.

questions.question: What is a key difference between reporting and performance analytics?
options: Performance Analytics contains snapshots of data taken over time; Reporting shows only the data as it is, at the moment the report is run.
Performance Analytics can show trends; Reports cannot.
Reports can be run on a scheduled basis; Performance Analytics cannot.
Performance Analytics data can be published to Dashboards; Reports cannot.
Performance Analytics shows KPIs; Reporting does not.
questions.explanation: The fundamental distinction is time: Performance Analytics collects scheduled snapshots (scores) so you can see how a value changes over days, weeks, and months, while a Report shows only the live data at the instant it runs (A). Option B is a tempting half-truth - reports can show point-in-time trends to a limited degree, but only Performance Analytics is built on historical snapshot data, which is the precise, defining difference.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Performance Analytics vs. Reporting

questions.question: While showing a customer their incident form, they ask to change the priority values to display their internal terminology P1, P2, P3, P4. They want it to be consistent across all tasks. How would you do that? Right click on priority and select what?
questions.explanation: Right-clicking the Priority field label and selecting Configure Choices (shown here as 'Configure Options', F) opens the Choices list for that field so you can relabel the values. Because Priority is defined on the Task table and Incident extends Task, editing the choices at that level makes the P1 - P4 labels consistent across all task-based tables, which is exactly what the customer asked for.

questions.question: Your customer would like to create a new template to notify users who are Affected by network Outages at their site. Which module would you use to create a new notification?
questions.explanation: Notifications are created and managed under System Notification > Email > Notifications, where you define the trigger (event, record condition), recipients (who/whom), and the message template (A). System Properties controls email account/server settings rather than individual notifications, and User Preferences only governs whether a single user receives email, not the creation of a notification record.

questions.question: When designing a flow, how do you reference data from a record, in that flow?
options: Drag the table icon onto the flow definition
Use the condition builder to specify the desired values
Specify the source table on the data pill related list
Drag the data pill onto the flow definition
Add the table reference using the slush bucket
questions.explanation: In Flow Designer, output values from a trigger or earlier action are exposed as data pills, and you reference them by dragging the data pill into the input field where you want that value used (D). There is no 'data pill related list' or slush-bucket method for this - the drag-and-drop data pill is the core mechanism for passing record data through a flow.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Use data pills in Flow Designer

questions.question: On the reports page, what sections allow you to see which reports are visible to different audiences? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: On the Reports list, reports are grouped by visibility audience: My reports (visible only to you), Group (shared with specific users/groups), Global (visible org-wide), and All (every report you can see). Those four sections are A, C, F, and I.

questions.question: Which tool is used to define relationships between fields in an import set table and a target table?
questions.explanation: A Transform Map defines how each field on the staging import set table maps to a field on the target table, and it is also where coalesce fields and field/script transformations are configured (D). The other names are not real ServiceNow import tools - a Schema Map exists for visualizing table relationships but is not used to map import fields to a target.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Import set key concepts (Transform Map)

questions.question: Which ServiceNow capability provides assistance to help users obtain information, make decisions, and perform common work tasks via a messaging interface?
questions.explanation: Virtual Agent is ServiceNow's conversational bot that uses pre-built topics and NLU to help users get information, make decisions, and complete tasks through a chat/messaging interface (C). 'Chat bot' (B) is only a generic description, not the named platform capability, and Agent Workspace is the interface human agents use rather than the automated assistant the question describes.

questions.question: Which feature allows you to automate business logic for a particular application or process such as approvals, tasks notifications, and record operations?
questions.explanation: A Flow (built in Flow Designer) automates business logic for a process - generating approvals, creating tasks, sending notifications, and performing record operations - using triggers and actions. Since 'Flow Diagrams' is not a real feature, the correct answer is Flows (A).
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Flows in Flow Designer

questions.question: From a form, what would you click to add additional fields to the form? (Choose two.)
options: Right click on header > Add > Field
Right click on header > Configure > UX Dashboard
questions.explanation: From a form's context menu you reach Configure > Form Layout (a slushbucket/text-based editor) or Configure > Form Design (a drag-and-drop builder); both let you add fields to the form. The correct pair is therefore B and C.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Form layout and design

questions.question: What is the name of the table relationship, where two or more tables are related in a bi-directional relationship, so that the related records are visible from both tables in a related list?
questions.explanation: A Many-to-Many (M2M) relationship lets records on two tables relate to each other in both directions, and ServiceNow stores the links in a hidden M2M table so the related records appear in a related list on both parent forms (B). A One-to-Many is unidirectional via a reference field, a Database View joins tables for reporting only (read-only, no related lists), and table Extension is inheritance rather than a relationship.

questions.question: On a form header, what is the three bar icon called?
questions.explanation: The three horizontal lines in the form header are commonly called the hamburger icon, and clicking it opens the form context menu of additional actions (C). While 'Additional Actions / Context Menu' (B) describes what the menu does, the question specifically asks the name of the three-bar icon, which is the hamburger.

questions.question: Group records are stored in which table?
questions.explanation: Groups are stored in the Group table with the platform name sys_user_group (B), following the sys_ convention for core platform tables and pairing with sys_user (users) and sys_user_grmember (membership). The sn_, s_, and u_ prefixed names are not the core group table.

questions.question: What function do you use to add buttons, links, and context menu items on forms and lists?
questions.explanation: UI Actions create the clickable controls - buttons, form links, list buttons, and context menu items - on forms and lists, and they can run client- or server-side script (C). UI Policies (A) dynamically control field state (mandatory, read-only, visible) but do not add buttons or menu items.

questions.question: On a business rule, the when setting determines at what point the rule executes. What are the options for specifying that timing?
questions.explanation: The Business Rule 'When' field has exactly four values - Before, After, Async, and Display - which control whether the rule runs before/after the database operation, asynchronously via a scheduled job, or as the form loads (A). Insert/Update/Delete/Query (C) are the operation checkboxes that say which database actions trigger the rule, not the 'When' timing options.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - How business rules work

questions.question: What are different types of data sources, which may be imported into ServiceNow? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: ServiceNow data sources can pull from local file uploads (XML, CSV, Excel), a JDBC connection to an external database, and an LDAP connection to a directory server - A, D, and F are standard import source types. The source rounds the set out with DataHub (C); 'Implementation Spoke' and 'Network Server' are not data-source types.

questions.question: What are the components that make up a filter condition? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Every filter condition is built from three parts: a Field (the column to evaluate), an Operator (such as is, contains, greater than), and a Value to compare against - A, C, and E. 'Column' overlaps with Field but is not the term ServiceNow uses for the condition component, and 'Match Criteria' (AND/OR) joins multiple conditions rather than forming one.

questions.question: When impersonating a user for testing purposes, what is the best way to return the instance, logged in with your user account?
options: Turn your computer off and on again
questions.explanation: When impersonating a user, you click the profile/avatar menu and select End Impersonation to return to your own logged-in session. This is the built-in mechanism for exiting impersonation, making option C correct.

questions.question: What controls the publishing and retiring process for knowledge articles?
questions.explanation: Each knowledge base is assigned publish and retire Workflows that define the approval and state transitions for its articles. ServiceNow ships defaults such as Approval Publish, Instant Publish, and Instant Retire, and you can clone and customize them. The controlling mechanism is Workflows (D).

questions.question: What type of query allows you to filter list data using normal words, instead of the condition builder?
questions.explanation: Natural Language Query (NLQ) lets users filter a list by typing plain-language phrases such as 'open incidents assigned to me' instead of building conditions in the condition builder (A). The other options are not real ServiceNow list-filtering features - Predictive Intelligence is an ML framework for classification/similarity, not a typed list query.

questions.question: Tables may have a one to many relationships. From the service catalog, what are examples of tables having a one to many relationships? (Choose three.)
options: One Approval can have many Requests
One Request can have many Requested Items
One Requested Item can have many Approvals
One Requested Item can have many Catalog Tasks
One Cart can have many Requests
questions.explanation: In the Service Catalog data model, a Request (REQ) can contain many Requested Items (RITM); each RITM can have many Approvals; and each RITM can have many Catalog Tasks (SCTASK). A cart, however, generates one Request at checkout, so the correct trio is B, C, and D.

questions.question: On a filter condition, which component is always a choice list?
questions.explanation: A condition row consists of a Field, an Operator, and a Value. The Field and Value vary by type, but the Operator is always presented as a choice list (is, is not, contains, etc.). The correct term is Operator (A).

questions.question: A role is defined as what?
options: A set of user access policies
A set of access control rules
questions.explanation: A role is a named collection of permissions (granted via the ACLs and other access associated with it) that you assign to users or groups to grant access in bulk (A). It is not itself the set of access control rules (D) - ACLs reference roles, but the role is the container of permissions, and assigning the role is what conveys access.

questions.question: A user is complaining that they are seeing a blank page, when they click create new, from your custom Inventory application. You have confirmed that they can see the Inventory application, and the create new module on the application navigator. What could be the cause of this issue?
options: Create New module has a broken link
User should be using Chrome instead of Explorer for their browser
User has read role, but not the write role on the Inventory table
questions.explanation: If the user can navigate to the module but gets a blank form on Create New, the most likely cause is that they have read access to the Inventory table but lack the write (create) role, so ACLs suppress the field/form and nothing renders (D). A broken module link or timed-out session would typically produce a different error, and the module is confirmed visible, ruling those out.

questions.question: What resource can you use to view details of the tables and configuration items (CIs) associated with a particular use case?
options: Common Service Data Model (CSDM) product view
questions.explanation: The Common Service Data Model (CSDM) product view documents the recommended tables and CI classes for each use case, showing how data should be modeled across the CMDB (D). The 'CI Use Case Modeler' and 'CMDB Use Case Modeler' are not actual ServiceNow resources, making CSDM the correct reference for use-case-based table and CI guidance.

questions.question: A manager wants to view a snapshot of month-end sales performance data, as compared to sales targets. In addition, the manager wants to be able to see those monthly numbers trended over time, and forecasted into the future. What capability do you suggest for this manager?
options: Scheduled Reports, a custom snapshot table, and a Trend report
Scheduled Reports, a custom snapshot table, and a Projection report
questions.explanation: Performance Analytics is purpose-built for exactly this: it captures periodic snapshots (scores), compares them against targets, trends them over time, and can forecast future values (D). The build-it-yourself options using scheduled reports and custom snapshot tables (A, C) would crudely approximate this but are far more fragile, and a single KPI (E) is just one indicator, not the trending-and-forecasting solution.

questions.question: What are advantages of using Flow Designer? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Flow Designer's advantages are that its reusable, no-code building blocks reduce technical debt (C), it minimizes manual scripting through configurable actions (D), and spokes provide smooth integration with third-party systems (E). The remaining options invert its purpose - Flow Designer is aimed at reducing custom code, not enabling complicated scripting (B) or catering primarily to advanced developers (A).

questions.question: Your customer requires that they be able to monitor which users are performing impersonations in their instance. What would you do to meet that requirement?
options: Add the role Log Write [sn_log_write] to the Impersonator Group
Create user update set for impersonation tracking
From User icon, select Elevate Roles
On the Impersonator role record, right click and select Create Log
questions.explanation: Setting the system property glide.sys.log_impersonation to true causes ServiceNow to write a log entry every time a user starts or stops impersonating someone, giving administrators an auditable record of impersonation activity (C). The other options are fabricated mechanisms - there is no Impersonator Group role or 'Create Log' action that produces this tracking.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Impersonate a user / impersonation logging

questions.question: When a flow runs an action, it generates a runtime value, which stays the same for the duration of the flow. What is the name of this runtime value?
questions.explanation: Action and trigger outputs in a flow are surfaced as data pills, and the value carried by a data pill is established when that step runs and remains available (unchanged) for the rest of the flow's execution - hence the 'data pill runtime value' (D). The other names are not Flow Designer terms for these persisted runtime outputs.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Data pills in Flow Designer

questions.question: The wait time for end users is based on the round- trip between the client and the server. What activities are included in the round-trips?
questions.explanation: A client-server round trip consists of the client sending a Request to the server and the server returning a Response; the user's perceived wait time is the sum of these two legs plus processing (A). The other pairs describe database or form operations rather than the network request/response cycle that defines a round trip.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Client script best practices

questions.question: When importing data, what happens to imported rows, if no coalesce field is specified?
options: All rows are rejected from the import, as coalesce field is required.
All rows are treated as new records. No existing records are updated.
Duplicate rows are rejected from the import.
All rows are treated as new records, but errors will be flagged in the import log.
questions.explanation: Coalescing is what matches incoming rows to existing target records. Without a coalesce field, the transform has no key to match on, so all rows are treated as new and inserted - re-running the import would create duplicates. This makes option B correct.

questions.question: What is the most common role that has access to almost all platform features, functions, and data?
questions.explanation: The System Administrator role, whose internal name is simply 'admin', grants access to nearly all platform features, applications, functions, and data. The correct option is System Administrator [admin] (D).

questions.question: What feature do you use to specify which users are able to access a service catalog item?
questions.explanation: User Criteria is the feature that defines which users (by role, group, department, location, etc.) can view and order a given Service Catalog item or category (D). It is applied through the item's Available For / Not Available For lists; the other options are not the supported mechanism for catalog item access control.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Apply user criteria to catalog items

questions.question: Which component of a table contains a piece of data for one record?
questions.explanation: In a ServiceNow table, a record is a row and a Field is the column that holds one piece of data for that record (B) - for example, the Short description field on an incident. 'Element' is the dictionary's internal column name for a field definition, but the component that stores a single data value on a record is the field.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Tables and fields (data dictionary)

questions.question: What type of field has a drop down list, from which you can pick from pre-defined options?
questions.explanation: A Choice field presents a predefined drop-down list of values that the user selects from, with the options stored as choice records for that field (A). 'Picker', 'Drop down', and 'Option' are not ServiceNow field types - the field type that renders a fixed selectable list is the Choice field.

questions.question: User records are stored in which table?
questions.explanation: User records live in the User table whose platform name is sys_user (A), consistent with the sys_ prefix on core platform tables. The sn_, u_, and s_ prefixed names are not the core user table - sys_user is where every user account is stored.

questions.question: What ServiceNow feature can be triggered by events, and is used to inform users about activities or updates in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: Events are signals raised in the platform; Notifications subscribe to those events (or to record conditions) and send email/messages to inform users about activities or updates. Since the question asks for the feature that informs users, the answer is Notifications (A).
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Email notifications and events

questions.question: Which ServiceNow capability allows you to provide knowledge articles, via a conversational messaging interface?
questions.explanation: Virtual Agent is the conversational, chatbot-style interface that can surface knowledge articles and run automated topics for users (B). Agent Assist helps a live human fulfiller find relevant knowledge while working a record, so it is agent-facing rather than the conversational self-service channel described here.

questions.question: Which role can manage multiple knowledge bases?
questions.explanation: The knowledge_admin role can administer Knowledge Management across the platform, including managing multiple knowledge bases (D). The knowledge_manager role, by contrast, is scoped to managing a specific knowledge base, and the other listed role names are not standard out-of-the-box Knowledge roles.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the differences between a client script and a business rule?
options: A Client Script executes before a record is loaded and a Business Rule executes after a record is loaded
A Client Script executes on the server and a Business Rule executes on the client
A Client Script executes on the client and a Business Rule executes on the server
A Client Script executes before a record is loaded and a Business Rule executes after a record is updated
questions.explanation: Client Scripts run in the user's web browser (the client side) and react to form events such as load, change, and submit, while Business Rules run on the server when records are queried, inserted, updated, or deleted (C). Option B reverses these execution contexts, and the timingbased options conflate the two without correctly stating where each runs.

questions.question: What are benefits of assigning work tasks to a group, rather than to an individual? (Choose four.)
options: Group members can choose their tasks from My Groups Work
Groups can assign tasks to users based on on-call schedules
Site support members can pick tasks, based on Location
Groups can assign tasks to users based on skills
Group members can avoid tasks, which are nearing SLA breach
Groups can assign tasks to users based on availability
questions.explanation: Assigning to a group lets the platform distribute work intelligently - by on-call schedules (B), by location for site support (C), by skills (D), and by availability (F). Option E is wrong because group assignment is meant to improve coverage, not to let members dodge work that is about to breach an SLA, which would undermine service levels.

questions.question: What ServiceNow feature allows you to include data from a secondary related table on a report?
questions.explanation: Dot-walking follows a reference field from one table to a field on the related table, letting you pull in columns from a secondary table when building a report (B). ServiceNow abstracts the database layer, so administrators do not write raw SQL or manual joins to traverse related records - they dot-walk through reference fields instead.

questions.question: What attributes can you manage, using System Properties > Basic Configuration UI16? (Choose five.)
questions.explanation: The Basic Configuration UI16 properties page lets you brand the interface: set the browser tab title (A), module text color (B), base system theme (D), header background color (G), and banner image (H). Preferred browser, font style, and animation style are not configurable from this page - they are user/browser settings or not exposed there.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Configure UI16 logo, colors, and system defaults

questions.question: Which field (Or fields) is used as a unique key during imports?
questions.explanation: During a transform, the Coalesce field (or combination of fields) acts as the unique key that the system matches against to decide whether to update an existing record or insert a new one (B). 'Match Fields' and 'Key Fields' are not the ServiceNow term, and Sys IDs are auto-generated identifiers rather than the import match key you configure on a field map.

questions.question: You are asked to create an option in the service catalog, which will allow a user to click get help and describe the issue they are having. These forms should create incident records, which are automatically routed to the service desk. Which method would you use?
questions.explanation: A Record Producer is a catalog-style form that creates a record on a specified table - here, an Incident - so it is the right tool for a 'Get Help' form that opens and routes incidents (A). A standard Catalog Item generates a request/RITM for fulfillment rather than directly creating an incident, and Order Guides and Content Items serve different catalog purposes.

questions.question: What is the result of the order in which access controls are evaluated?
options: Ensures user has access to the fields in a table, before considering their access to the table
Ensures user can get to work as quickly as possible
Ensures user has access to the application, before evaluating access to a module within the application
Ensures user has access to a table, before evaluating access to a field in the table
questions.explanation: ServiceNow evaluates ACLs from the table (row) level down to the field (column) level - a user must first pass the table-level access control before any field-level rule is even considered (D). Option A reverses this order; you cannot be granted field access on a table you cannot reach in the first place.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - How access control rules are evaluated

questions.question: Which tool graphically displays an infrastructure view for a configuration item (CI) and its relationship with other CIs?
questions.explanation: Dependency View (formerly the BSM map) renders a graphical, infrastructure-level picture of a CI and the upstream/downstream CIs it relates to (B). A Schema Map diagrams table relationships in the data model, and a Database View joins tables for reporting - neither visualizes CIto-CI infrastructure relationships.

questions.question: What are examples of core tables in the ServiceNow platform?
questions.explanation: User (sys_user), Task, and Incident are all core, out-of-the-box tables that ship with the Now Platform (C). The other options list a mix of feature names and non-existent table names that are not part of the platform's core data model.

questions.question: Which tab on the knowledge base record, would you use to identify the sets of users who are able to read articles in that knowledge base?
questions.explanation: On a knowledge base record, the Can Read tab is where you attach the User Criteria that define which sets of users are allowed to read the articles (D). The Cannot Read tab does the opposite (denies access), and the other tab names listed do not exist on the knowledge base form.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Apply user criteria to a knowledge base

questions.question: What are the main components of the form design interface? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The drag-and-drop Form Designer is organized into a Page Header (the toolbar/title area), a Field Navigator (the panel listing available fields to drag on), and the Form Layout (the canvas where you arrange fields and sections) - B, C, and E. 'Field Layout' and 'Field Picker' are not the named components of the Form Design interface.

questions.question: What is used to determine user access to knowledge bases or a knowledge article?
questions.explanation: User Criteria are reusable records that specify which users (by role, group, company, department, or location) can read or contribute to knowledge bases and articles (D). The other options are not the access mechanism - there is no Privacy Settings or Read Access Flag concept for Knowledge, and the listed role names are not how article visibility is controlled.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - User criteria for knowledge

questions.question: What are the three key tables in an enterprise CMDB? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The CMDB is anchored by three tables: cmdb (the base configuration management table), cmdb_ci (the Configuration Item table that most CI classes extend), and cmdb_rel_ci (which stores the relationships between CIs) - A, C, and F. The sn_-prefixed and _bak options are not real core CMDB tables.

questions.question: What is the best practice related to using the default update set for moving customizations between instances?
options: Merge Default update sets before moving between instances
Submit Default update set to application repository
You should not use the Default Update sets for moving between instances
Keep Default update set to maximum of 20 records, for troubleshooting purposes
questions.explanation: ServiceNow's best practice is to leave the Default update set in place and create named update sets for your changes, so you should not use Default to move customizations between instances (C). The Default set is the always-present catch-all for the instance; the other options describe actions that are not recommended for it.

questions.question: On what part of the ServiceNow instance, would you find the option to impersonate user?
questions.explanation: The Impersonate User option is found in the User menu (the user/profile menu at the top-right of the banner frame), where admins can also elevate roles and log out (D). The Application Navigator, content frame, and individual modules do not host the impersonation control.

questions.question: Which application is used primarily to load data into ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: The System Import Sets application is the primary tool for loading external data into ServiceNow - you create a data source, load the staging import set table, and run a transform map onto the target table (B). The other application names are not the standard out-of-the-box module used for importing data.

questions.question: If a knowledge base has no access details specified, what users are able to read articles in that knowledge base?
options: Any user with an article's permalink
questions.explanation: When a knowledge base has no User Criteria restricting access, the default behavior is that any active user can read its articles (C). Access becomes restricted only once you add Can Read / Cannot Read user criteria; without them, the knowledge base is open to all authenticated users rather than locked down to a specific role.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - User criteria for knowledge

questions.question: A department manager asks an analyst to build some reports. Where do you recommend the analyst start?
questions.explanation: To build a report, the analyst navigates to Reports > Create New, which opens the Report Designer where you pick the data source, type, and style (E). The other paths point to dashboards, Performance Analytics, or self-service views that are not the entry point for authoring a new report.

questions.question: What are the steps for applying an update set to an instance?
questions.explanation: On the target instance you Retrieve the completed update set from the source, Preview it to detect collisions and validate the changes, and then Commit it to apply the customizations (A). The other sequences mix in import-set terminology (Transform) or invented steps that are not part of the update set workflow.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Retrieve, preview, and commit update sets

questions.question: When importing spreadsheet data into ServiceNow, in which step does the data get written to the receiving table?
questions.explanation: After data is staged in the import set table, running the transform map maps and writes the records into the target table. The UI action that performs this is 'Run Transform' (sometimes shown simply as Transform), making option A the step where data reaches the receiving table.

questions.question: What would you do, on a list, if you wanted to show the records in groups, based on the column category? (Choose two.)
options: On list Context Menu, select Group By > Category
On the Filter Menu, select Group By > Category
Click Group On icon, select Category
On Navigator Filter, type tablename.group.category and press enter
On the Category column title, click Context menu > Group By Category
questions.explanation: You can group a list either from the list (title) context menu by choosing Group By > Category (A), or from the column header's context menu on the Category column by choosing Group By (E). The Filter menu, a 'Group On' icon, and a navigator-filter syntax are not valid ways to group a list.

questions.question: What is the definition of a group?
options: A collection of subject matter experts
questions.explanation: In ServiceNow a group is simply a collection of users who share a common purpose, such as fulfilling a certain type of task or receiving the same notifications (C). It is not the same as a department (an HR/organizational construct) and is not limited to subject matter experts - any set of users can form a group.

questions.question: Which ServiceNow utility provides a modern interactive graphical interface to visualize configuration items and their relationship?
questions.explanation: The CI Class Manager / CI Class Map provides a modern, interactive graphical interface for browsing the CMDB CI class hierarchy and the relationships between configuration item classes (D). Dependency View visualizes a specific CI's runtime relationships, whereas the CI Class Map is the newer utility for exploring the class model itself.

questions.question: You have been asked to configure a form so an employee could order a tablet and select the standard accessory options to purchase with it. These standard options are: carrying case, screen cleaner, tablet stand, and screen protector. What approach would you take? (Choose three.)
options: Create Catalog item for the tablet, and on the form, add a check box variable for each accessory option.
Create Catalog item for the tablet, and add a variable set to the form, for the accessory options.
Create one Catalog item for each: tablet, carrying case, screen cleaner, tablet stand, and screen protector.
Create a Records producer, and on the form, add a check box variable for each accessory option.
On shopping Cart configuration, select option to show the Add Accessories button.
questions.explanation: Valid catalog approaches are to build one catalog item for the tablet with a checkbox variable per accessory (A), to build the tablet item and attach a reusable variable set holding the accessory options (B), or to create a separate catalog item for the tablet and each accessory (C). A Record Producer (D) creates a single record rather than an orderable product, and there is no 'Add Accessories' shopping-cart toggle (E).
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Service Catalog variables and variable sets

questions.question: The ServiceNow platform supports a wide variety of plus-and-play application. You can choose from the included workflow or build your own workflow. Which of following these workflows are included in the platform?
questions.explanation: ServiceNow's product families are organized around IT Workflows, Employee Workflows, and Customer Workflows (plus Creator Workflows) - so A, E, and F are the included workflow categories. 'Infrastructure,' 'Federal,' and 'Manufacturing' are not the names of ServiceNow's standard workflow product lines.

questions.question: What service catalog feature do you use to organize items into logical groups?
questions.explanation: Service Catalog Categories group catalog items into logical, navigable groupings (e.g., Hardware, Software) to help users find what they need. Variable sets, by contrast, bundle reusable variables within an item. The feature for organizing items is Categories (D).

questions.question: A customer requests the following data quality measures be added: 1. Incident numbers should be read- only on all lists and forms, for all users. 2. Short description field should be mandatory, on all records, across all applications, on insert. Which type of policy would you use to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: A Data Policy enforces mandatory and read-only field rules at the data layer, so the rules apply everywhere data enters the table - lists, forms, imports, and web services - regardless of application (A). UI Policies only affect forms in the browser, and the other listed policy types are not real ServiceNow features.

questions.question: When creating a new notification, what must you define? (Choose three.)
options: What is the content of the notification
Under what conditions is the notification sent
Settings for handling inactive user accounts
questions.explanation: Every notification needs three things defined: when it fires (the conditions/trigger), who it goes to (the recipients), and what it says (the content/message) - A, C, and D. A knowledge base association and inactive-account handling are not part of configuring a notification record.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Create an email notification

questions.question: Which type of ServiceNow script runs on the web browser?
questions.explanation: Client Scripts execute in the user's web browser and respond to form events like onLoad, on‐ Change, and onSubmit (D). Server-side logic such as business rules runs on the application server, not the browser; 'Local script' and 'Database script' are not ServiceNow script types.

questions.question: How would you distinguish between a base class table and a parent class table?
options: Base Class tables always have tables extended from them, Parent tables do not have tables extended from them.
Base Class table is not extended from another table. Parent class tables may be extended from another table.
Extended tables can be extended from Parent tables or Base tables, but they cannot be extended from both.
Extended tables are always extended from Parent tables, Extended tables are usually extended from Base tables,
questions.explanation: A Base Class table sits at the top of a hierarchy and is not extended from any other table, while a Parent table is simply any table that has children extending it - and a parent can itself be extended from a higher table (B). The distinction is about position in the extension chain: base = the root, parent = has descendants.

questions.question: What types of entities can receive task assignments, in ServiceNow? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Tasks are assigned through the Assignment group and Assigned to fields, so the entities that can receive a task are Groups and Users (A and B). Departments are organizational records used for reporting and user criteria, and 'Teams' is not a task-assignment target in core ServiceNow.

questions.question: What are examples of UI actions relating to forms? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: On a form, UI Actions render as Form Buttons, Form Context Menu items, and Form Links (the related links at the bottom of the form) - A, C, and D. 'Form View' is a layout/display configuration and 'Form Columns' relate to field arrangement, neither of which is a UI Action control.

questions.question: Which is the most efficient way to move large amounts of data between instances?
questions.explanation: For moving actual data records between instances, exporting to XML lets you capture many records and re-import them on the target instance (B). Update Sets are designed for configuration and customizations, not bulk data, so they are the wrong tool for moving data; the other export formats listed are not the standard data-transfer mechanism.

questions.question: When a custom table is created, which access control rules are automatically created? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: Creating a new table auto-generates ACLs for the four CRUD operations the platform secures at the row/field level: create, read, write, and delete (A, B, D, F). ServiceNow uses 'write' rather than 'update' for the modify operation, and 'execute' applies to UI actions/script operations, not the default table CRUD ACLs.

questions.question: What does natural language query allow you to do on a list?
options: Automatically select a filter, based on keywords
Filter list by typing in a phrase
Predict the filter desired by the user
Set list filter, using audible commands
questions.explanation: Natural Language Query lets a user type a plain-language phrase that the platform interprets into a list filter based on keywords (A). The keyed answer is A, though option B ('Filter list by typing in a phrase') describes essentially the same behavior; NLQ is text-driven, so the 'speak'/'audible command' options (D, E) are incorrect.

questions.question: On the knowledge base record, which tab would you use to define which users are able to write articles to the knowledge base?
questions.explanation: On a knowledge base record, the Can Contribute tab holds the User Criteria that determine which users may create and edit (author) articles in that knowledge base (C). The Can Read tab governs viewing access only; the other tab names listed do not exist on the knowledge base form.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Apply user criteria to a knowledge base

questions.question: When would you use the following steps? 1, homepage admin > pages 2. Right click on homepage record 3. Select unioad portal page
options: To publish a Homepage to the Portal
o To add a Homepage to an update set
questions.explanation: Homepages and other portal pages are stored as data, not configuration, so they are not automatically captured in update sets. Using Homepage Admin > Pages and the 'Unload Portal Page' action manually exports the page record into the current update set so it can be moved between instances (D). The action is about packaging the page for migration, not publishing, retiring, or deleting it.

questions.question: What is the platform name for the group table?
questions.explanation: The Group table's database name is sys_user_group (shown here as 'SyS_USer_group' with odd casing) - option A. Table names are case-insensitive in practice, so the correct value is sys_user_group, not sys_group or sys_groups. The Group table is closely tied to the User table, which is why it carries the sys_user_ prefix.

questions.question: When selecting the target table for an import, which tables can you select? (Choose three.)
options: Tables within the existing application scope
Tables which allow write access to other applications
questions.explanation: When choosing a transform target you can select tables in the global scope (A), tables in your current application scope (B), and tables in other scopes that explicitly allow write access via their application access settings (D). You cannot target tables 'outside of ServiceNow,' and you choose a single destination table rather than dot-walking to related tables (E).
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Transform maps and target tables

questions.question: From a form, what would you click, to modify the order of the fields on the form? (Choose two.)
options: Right click on header > Configure > Form Design
Right click on header > Configure > UX Dashboard
questions.explanation: You can change field order either through the classic Form Layout editor (Context Menu > Configure > Form Layout) (A) or through the drag-and-drop Form Design interface (right-click the header > Configure > Form Design) (C). The other paths reference menus that do not exist for editing field arrangement.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Form Designer and Form Layout

questions.question: On a form header, what icon would you click to access template features?
questions.explanation: Template features (apply template, save as template, manage templates) are reached from the More options menu - the three-dots (...) additional actions icon on the form header (B). The paper clip is for attachments, so it manages files rather than templates.

questions.question: The report designer contains different sections for configuring your report. Which section is used to adjust the look of your report, including colors, files, and legend layout?
questions.explanation: In the Report Designer, the Style section controls the visual appearance of a report - colors, fonts, titles, and legend layout (C). The Configure section defines the data and grouping, while Style is purely about how that data is presented, which is what the question describes.

questions.question: While on an incident record, how would you add a tag for "special handling" to the record?
options: Click on the More options (...) icon, click Add Tag, type Special Handling, press enter
On the Special Handling field, check the box
On the Tag field, select Special Handling from the choice list
Click on the Context menu, select Add Tag, type Special Handling, press enter
questions.explanation: Tags are added from the form's More options (...) menu by choosing Add Tag and typing the label, such as Special Handling (A). Tags are free-form metadata you attach to records, so there is no dedicated 'Special Handling' field or fixed choice list - ruling out B and C.

questions.question: Which best describes a field in a ServiceNow table?
options: A field is a table cell that stores data
A field is a table row
A field is an item that appears in a menu list
A field is a record in a table
questions.explanation: A table is a collection of records, each record is a row, and each field is a column/cell within that row that holds one piece of data. Option C describes a choice list value shown in a dropdown, not a field, so the correct description is A.

questions.question: WHILE TESTING A CATALOG ITEM FOR ORDERING AN EXPENSIVE COMPUTER, THE MANDATORY APPROVAL IS BEING SKIPPED FOR REQUESTER BOB, SMITH, BUT NOT FOR ANY OF THE OTHER REQUESTERS. WHAT COULD EXPLAIN THE ISSUE?
options: There is a business rule, excluding Bob.Smith from any approvals.
Bob Smith does not have a delegate set up on his account,
The Bob Smith user account, does not have a manager specified.
The manager does not have a delegate assigned,
questions.explanation: If approval is skipped only for one specific user while working for everyone else, a targeted automation is the likely cause - a business rule that explicitly excludes Bob Smith from approvals (A). A missing manager (C) would typically cause the approval to fail or stall for that user, not silently skip, and VIP status or delegate settings do not bypass a mandatory approval.

questions.question: What capability allows users to create dashboards with widgets to visualize data over time in order to identify areas of improvement?
questions.explanation: Performance Analytics captures scored data on a schedule and displays it on dashboards with widgets, letting users track trends over time and spot areas for improvement (B). Standard Reporting shows current/point-in-time data and cannot natively trend historical snapshots the way Performance Analytics does.

questions.question: When building an extended table from a base table, which fields do you need to create? (Choose two.)
options: The mandatory fields for the base table.
The reference fields for the base table.
The fields that are not in the base table.
The fields that are specific to the extended table.
questions.explanation: An extended table automatically inherits all of the parent (base) table's fields, so you only create the new fields the child needs - those that are not already in the base table (C) and those specific to the extended table (D). Re-creating the base table's mandatory or reference fields would be redundant because they are inherited.

questions.question: On a form, one type of field shows a small preview icon beside its value that, when clicked, opens a preview (a peek) of the record it points to. Which type of field is this?
questions.explanation: The small information (i) icon next to a populated field, shown here beside the Caller field, marks a Reference field - clicking it opens a preview of the referenced record without leaving the form. Reference fields store a pointer (sys_id) to a record on another table, which is why they offer this peek-ahead preview. The other terms are not ServiceNow field types.

questions.question: How would you navigate to the schema map for a table?
options: System Dictionary > Show Schema Map; Select Table
System Definition > Tables; Select Table; Go to Related links and click Show Schema Map
System Definition > Show Schema Map; Select Table
System Definition > Dictionary: Select Table; Go to Related links and click Show Schema Map
questions.explanation: The Schema Map is reached by opening System Definition > Tables, selecting the table record, and using the Related Links section to click Show Schema Map (B). The Schema Map then renders the table plus the tables it references and extends. There is no standalone 'Show Schema Map' module hanging directly off System Definition, which rules out C.

questions.question: Your customer has a human resources knowledge base, which is only accessible to members of the human resources department. A new procedure regarding employee quarterly reviews needs to be published to the quarterly review category of the HR knowledge base, but should only be visible for HR managers. How would you meet this requirement?
options: On the Knowledge Base, add User Criteria with a Manager Can Read script to the Can Read list, publish article to any category
Add User Criteria for HR Manager Group on the Category's Can Read list
On the Knowledge Article, add an Access Control for HR Manager Group on the Can Read list, then publish article to any category.
Add User Criteria for HR Manager Group on the Can Read list of the article
questions.explanation: Knowledge access is controlled with User Criteria, and it can be applied at the knowledge base, category, or article level. Because the restriction must apply specifically to the quarterly review category, adding a User Criteria for the HR Manager group to that Category's Can Read list is the correct, most precise scope (B). Access Control rules (C) are not how knowledge visibility is managed, and an article-level criteria (D) is broader/less aligned than scoping at the category the question specifies.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - User Criteria for Knowledge

questions.question: When adding a related list to a form, you choose the related list from the list collector, what is an example of a related list you might see on the list collector? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Related lists are populated either from a reference field pointing back to the current record (shown with the arrow '->' notation, e.g. Catalog Task->Parent and Outage->Task number) or from a defined database relationship. The arrow notation indicates a related table whose field references this record, which is why B, C, and E are valid related-list entries. The '==' notation entries (A and D) are not how the list collector expresses a relatable list.

questions.question: Many actions are included with Flow Designer. What are some frequently used core actions? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: The standard Flow Designer core actions include Ask for Approval (B), Create Record (C), Look Up Record (F), and Wait for Condition (A). 'Wait for Match' (D) and 'Look for Update' (E) are not real core actions, so the correct four are A, B, C, F.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Flow Designer core actions

questions.question: A form displays information about one record at the top, for example a user, additional records, which are associated with that user, are displayed on tabs at the bottom of the form. What are those tabs called?
questions.explanation: Records associated with the current record appear at the bottom of the form as Related Lists, often rendered as tabs (D). For example, a User form can show the user's group memberships or assigned incidents as related lists. Related Links (C) are clickable actions/links, not tabs of associated records.

questions.question: What feature allows, you to limit who is able to contribute or read knowledge within a knowledge base?
questions.explanation: User Criteria is the Knowledge Management feature that defines who can read and who can contribute (write) to a knowledge base, based on attributes like role, group, department, company, or location (C). While roles and groups can be referenced inside a User Criteria record, the feature itself that governs Can Read / Can Contribute is User Criteria, not roles or groups alone.

questions.question: What features are available in knowledge management, to support continuous improvement on the knowledge articles? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: Knowledge Management supports article feedback and continuous improvement through reader interactions: adding Comments, marking an article as Helpful, Flagging an article for review, and Rating it with stars (B, D, E, F). 'Submit KB Errata' and a 'frowning icon' click are not standard knowledge feedback features.

questions.question: What section on the notes tab, shows the history of the work documented on the record?
questions.explanation: The Activity section (the activity stream / activity formatter) on the Notes tab displays a chronological history of the work documented on a record - work notes, comments, and tracked field changes (B). 'Journal' refers to the underlying field type that feeds the stream, not the displayed section, and Audit Log is a separate system record of field-level changes.

questions.question: In Flow Designer, where is the data from an action stored so it can be used in subsequent actions in the flow?
questions.explanation: In Flow Designer, the output of a trigger or action is exposed as a Data Pill - a draggable token holding that value, which you drop into later steps to reuse it (C). Data pills are how data flows from one action to the next. 'Data Element' and 'Data Trigger' are not Flow Designer terms for this.

questions.question: On what part of the ServiceNow instance, would you find the option to access applications, like incident management?
questions.explanation: The Application Navigator (the left-hand navigation pane) is where applications and their modules - such as Incident Management - are listed and opened (B). Favorites is only a personalized shortcut view within the navigator, and the Self Service module / Service Desk homepage are specific destinations, not the general application access point.

questions.question: For your implementation, the following tables are extended from each other: Incident table is extended from Task table, Super Incident table is extended from Incident table. In this situation, which tables are parent, child and base tables? (Choose five.)
options: Incident table is a Base table
Incident table is. a Parent table
Incident table is a Child table
Super Incident table is a Child table
Super Incident table is a Parent table
Super Incident table is a Base table
Task table is a Base table
Task table is a Parent table
Task table is a Child table
questions.explanation: Task is the Base table at the top of the hierarchy and is therefore also a Parent (G, H). Incident sits in the middle: it is a Child of Task and simultaneously a Parent of Super Incident (B, C). Super Incident is at the bottom, making it purely a Child (D).
