Super Incident cannot be a Base or Parent, and Incident is not the base since Task is above it.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Table extension and hierarchy

questions.question: When you set a policy that is applied to all data entered into the platform (UI, import sets, or web services), where does this policy run by default?
questions.explanation: A policy that must apply to every data entry channel - UI, Import Sets, and Web Services - has to run on the server, because Import Sets and Web Services bypass the browser entirely (B). This describes a Data Policy (or a server-side business rule), which enforces rules regardless of how the data arrives. Client-side logic only fires in the browser, so it could not cover imports or web service inserts.

questions.question: When moving a homepage or dashboard between instances, what must you remember?
options: Create a separate update set for them
They are automatically added to the update set
Manually add them to the update set
They cannot be moved via update set
questions.explanation: Homepages and dashboards are not tracked automatically by update sets, so you must manually add them - typically by using the 'Add to Update Set' related link or the Update Set Picker for unloaded records (C). Because they are data-style records rather than tracked configuration, leaving them to be captured automatically (B) would result in them being missed on the target instance.

questions.question: What tool is used to import data from various data sources, and map that data into ServiceNow tables?
questions.explanation: Import Sets are the tool for bringing data in from external data sources (spreadsheets, JDBC, files) into a staging table and then mapping/transforming it into a target ServiceNow table (A). Update Sets move configuration between instances, not external data, and 'Data Pack' / 'Transform Set' are not the correct tool names for this import process.

questions.question: Access controls are evaluated in this order: 1. Match object against table ACL 2. Match the object against field ACL within step 1 above, what order are the table ACLs evaluated?
options: Specific to general: Table.Field ACL, Parent Table.Field ACL, *.Field ACL
Bottom to top: Table ACL, Table.Field ACL, Parent Table. Field ACL
General to specific: Table ACL, Table.Field ACL, Parent Table, Field ACL
Top to bottom: Wildcard Table ACL, Parent Table ACL, Table ACL
Specific to general: Table ACL, Parent Table ACL, Wildcard (*) ACL
questions.explanation: Table-level ACLs are evaluated from most specific to most general: the table's own ACL first, then its parent table ACL, and finally the wildcard (*) 'any table' ACL (E). Access is granted only when the most specific matching rule passes, so the wildcard catch-all is checked last. The options describing field ACLs (A, C) are answering the wrong layer for this step.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - How access control rules are processed

questions.question: What are the three key tables in an enterprise CMDB? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The three foundational CMDB tables are cmdb (the base Configuration Item parent table), cmdb_ci (the base Configuration Item table where CIs are stored), and cmdb_rel_ci (which stores the relationships between CIs).

questions.question: On access control definitions, what are ways you can set the permissions on a table? (Choose three.)
options: Script that sets the answer variable to true or false
questions.explanation: An Access Control (ACL) grants access through three configurable mechanisms: required Roles, a scripted condition that sets the 'answer' variable to true/false, and a conditional expression (field-based condition) - C, D, E. Groups are not set directly on an ACL (you assign roles, and roles are granted to groups), and 'CRUD' names the operations being protected rather than a permission-granting mechanism.

questions.question: When importing data from a spreadsheet, which step defines where the incoming data columns will be written in the receiving table?
questions.explanation: The Transform Map is what defines which incoming import-set column maps to which field on the target table, controlling where each value lands (E). Loading data only stages the rows in the import set table; it is the transform map's field maps that determine the destination columns in the receiving table.

questions.question: What module enables an administrator to define destinations for imported data on any ServiceNow table?
questions.explanation: The Transform Map module lets an administrator define the destination table and field mappings for data staged in an import set, for any target table (B). The Schema Map (C) only visualizes table relationships, and 'Field Transform' / 'Import Map' are not the module used to set import destinations.

questions.question: When using the data pill picker, use which keys to dot-walk (6 fields in other tables?
questions.explanation: In the Data Pill Picker you dot-walk into referenced fields on related tables using the arrow keys - the right arrow drills into a reference field's table, and the left arrow steps back out (A). The other key combinations listed are not how the picker navigates into related-table fields.

questions.question: What table acts as a staging area for records imported from a data source?
questions.explanation: Imported records first land in an Import Set Row table (the import set table, descended from sys_import_set_row), which serves as the temporary staging area before transformation into the target table (C). 'Staging Table', 'Transform Table', and 'Temp Table' are not the actual ServiceNow object name for this staging area.

questions.question: Which modules can you use to create a new table? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: You can create a new table from the Tables & Columns module (System Definition > Tables & Columns, using Create Table) and from the Tables module (System Definition > Tables, then New) - A and D. The Schema Map visualizes existing tables, and the Dictionary manages field/table definitions rather than serving as the new-table creation module.

questions.question: When looking at a long list of records, you want to quickly filter, to show only those which have category of hardware. How might you do that?
options: On the list, locate and right click on the value Hardware, select Show Matching
Click Funnel ten, type Hardware and click enter
On the Category column header, right click and select Show > Hardware
Right dick on magnifier, type Hardware and click enter
On Breadcrumb, click > icon, type Hardware and click enter
questions.explanation: The fastest way to filter a list to one value is to right-click a cell containing that value and choose 'Show Matching', which instantly filters the list to records sharing that value (A). This contextual list action is the standard one-click filter; the other described gestures don't correspond to how list filtering works.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Filter a list (Show Matching)

questions.question: When managing tags, you can adjust who is able to see it. What are the visibility options? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: A tag's visibility can be set to Me (private to you), Groups and Users (shared with specific people), or Everyone (visible platform-wide) - B, C, E. 'Admins' and 'Roles and Permissions' are not the visibility choices offered when sharing a tag.

questions.question: Which one of the following describes the primary operations performed against tables in the ServiceNow platform?
questions.explanation: The primary table operations in ServiceNow are Create, Read, Write, and Delete (C) - the CRUD operations that Access Controls also secure (where Write covers update). The other options substitute non-operations like 'Rate', 'Upload', 'Capture', or 'Develop' that are not the core database actions.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - CRUD operations and ACLs

questions.question: What is the primary objective of the display business rule?
options: To monitor fields on a form, and provide feedback
To use a shared g_scratchpad object, which can be sent to the client, as part of the form
To set files to mandatory, hidden, and read-only
To define what happens on a form, when a particular fled changes
questions.explanation: A Display Business Rule runs server-side just before a form loads and its purpose is to populate the g_scratchpad object with server data so client scripts can use that information on the form (B). Setting fields mandatory/hidden/read-only is a UI Policy's job, and reacting to a specific field change is a Client Script's role - not the Display business rule.

questions.question: What icon do you use to change the icon and color on a favorite?
questions.explanation: To edit a favorite - including changing its icon and color - you click the Pencil (edit) icon, which opens the favorite's edit controls (C). The Star marks/creates a favorite, the Clock shows your history, so neither lets you customize the favorite's appearance.

questions.question: What access does a user need to be able to import articles to a knowledge base?
questions.explanation: To import (or otherwise create/author) articles in a knowledge base, a user must satisfy the 'Can Contribute' user criteria for that knowledge base (A). Contribute access is what grants write/import capability; the option text 'sn_knowledge_contripute' is a misspelled, non-existent role and 'Can import' is not the access term used.

questions.question: From a related list, what would a user click for personalize the layout of the columns?
questions.explanation: The Gear (settings/personalize) icon on a list or related list opens the Personalize List Columns dialog, where a user adds, removes, and reorders columns (D). The Magnifier toggles column search, and the Context Menu offers list actions, but it is the Gear icon that personalizes the column layout.

questions.question: On a filter condition, there is an element, which is based on the table, the user access rights, and columns on the table. What is this element called?
questions.explanation: In the condition builder, the first selector of each condition row is the Field - the choices available there are determined by the table you're on, the table's columns, and the user's access rights (C). While columns and fields are closely related, ServiceNow names this conditionbuilder element the Field selector, not 'Column' or 'Attribute'.

questions.question: What section on a task record would you use to see the most recent update made to a record?
questions.explanation: The Activity section (activity stream) on a task record presents the chronological record of updates, with the most recent entry shown so you can see what last changed (D). The Audit Log is a separate technical record of field changes rather than the form's at-a-glance update section, and 'Journal' is the underlying field type, not the displayed section.

questions.question: When looking at a long list of records, you want to quickly filter, to show only those which have short description containing email how might you do that?
options: Click List Magnifier to expand column search, on Short Description, type *email, click enter
Click List Magnifier to expand column search, on Short Description, type %email, click enter
Click List Magnifier to expand column search, on Short Description, type email, click enter
On Search box, select text, type email, click enter
questions.explanation: Clicking the List Magnifier opens the per-column search row; entering a value with a leading wildcard asterisk in the Short Description search box matches records that contain that substring anywhere in the field (A). The leading '*' makes it a 'contains' match rather than a 'starts with' match, which is why the wildcard form is correct over a plain term.

questions.question: What are the three key tables in an enterprise CMDB? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The three foundational CMDB tables are cmdb (base CI parent table), cmdb_ci (the Configuration Items table), and cmdb_rel_ci (CI relationships).

questions.question: Which roles are required to impersonate a user? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Two roles can impersonate users: admin (which can impersonate any user) and impersonator (which can impersonate only users who have granted it impersonation access) - A and E. 'sys_admin' and 'sys_user' are not valid impersonation roles, and security_admin governs elevated security settings rather than impersonation.

questions.question: How is a user defined in ServiceNow?
options: user is a record stored in the User Preference [Sys_user_preference] table
A User is a record stored in the Profile [sys_user_profile] table
A user is a field in the LDAP integration
A user is a record stored in the User [sys_user] table
questions.explanation: A user is a record stored in the User table, whose platform name is sys_user (D). The User Preference table stores per-user settings, not the user identity, and there is no 'sys_user_profile' table for users - so D is the only correct definition.

questions.question: In what order are access controls evaluated?
options: Field-level - most general to most specific: then Row-level - most specific to most general
Table-level - most specific to most general; then Row-level - most specific to most general
Table-level - most specific to most general; then Field-level - most specific to most general
Field-level - most specific to most general: then Table-level - most specific to most general
questions.explanation: Access Controls are matched table-level first and then field-level, with each level evaluated from the most specific rule to the most general, and both the matching table-level and field-level rules must be true for access. Option C captures this order; D incorrectly places field-level before table-level.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Access control evaluation order

questions.question: Tables may be set up with many to many relationships. What is a classic example of a scenario where the tables would have many to many relationships?
options: Requests can contain many items; and Items can be any item from the catalog.
Vendors can sell multiple products; and products can be sold by multiple vendors.
A Task can trigger many Workflows; and a Workflow can trigger many Tasks
A Configuration Item can belong to multiple Classes; and Classes can contain multiple Configuration Items.
questions.explanation: A many-to-many (M2M) relationship requires both sides to relate to multiple records on the other side, which the vendor/product example captures perfectly: each vendor sells many products and each product is sold by many vendors (B). The other scenarios are one-to-many or conceptually one-sided - for instance a CI belongs to a single class, not many - so they don't model a true M2M.

questions.question: On the form header, which icon do you use to access form templates?
questions.explanation: Form templates are reached from the form header's More Options menu (the additional-options '...' icon), which exposes Templates among other actions (D). The Paperclip attaches files, so it is unrelated to templates; the template controls live under the More Options menu.

questions.question: The employee on-boarding team has asked for a way for managers to order computers, monitors, business cards, and cell phones for new employees. How would you proceed to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: An Order Guide bundles several related catalog items into one guided, multi-step request, which is exactly what's needed to order computers, monitors, business cards, and phones together for a new hire (B). A Record Producer creates a single record on a table, and a Requested Item (RITM) is a line item generated by a request - neither bundles multiple catalog items the way an order guide does.

questions.question: When importing spreadsheet data into ServiceNow, what is the first step in the process?
questions.explanation: Using the Import XML/Load Data wizard, the first step is to create the Import Set, which establishes the staging table that will receive the spreadsheet rows (A). Coalescing and transform mapping happen later in the process, and there is no 'Data Scrubber' step in the standard import flow.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Load data using import sets

questions.question: After you create a new table, what is the best practice regarding the navigation pane? (Choose two.)
options: Set the filter condition on the Application Menu
Set the font style on both the Application Menu and the Module
Specify which Roles are able to see the Module
Specify which Roles are able to see the Application Menu
Create Application Menu with the same name as the table label
Create Module with the plural of the table label
questions.explanation: When exposing a new table in the Application Navigator, best practice is to restrict visibility by specifying which roles can see the Application Menu and which roles can see the Module (C and D), so only the right users see the new app and its links. Naming and font choices are cosmetic and not the security best practice the question targets.

questions.question: On the CI dependency view, what enables you to trace from an infrastructure item, like a server, to the services that are dependent on that server?
questions.explanation: The CI Dependency View visualizes CIs and the Relationships defined between them, and it is those CI relationships that let you trace from a server up to the services that depend on it (C). A Transform Map deals with data imports, not CI topology, so it has no role in dependency tracing.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - CI relationships and dependency views

questions.question: What options can you see, when you right click on a CI, from the CI dependency view map? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Right-clicking a CI in the dependency view opens context actions for that CI, including View Affected CIs, View Related Tasks, and View Recent Outages (A, B, C) - all of which relate the CI to operational impact. 'View Cases' and 'View Knowledge' are not standard CI dependency map context options.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - CI dependency view actions

questions.question: ServiceNow contains over 25 different report types. What are some of the types? (Choose five.)
questions.explanation: Valid ServiceNow report/visualization types include Pie, Speedometer, Horizontal Bar, Semi- Donut, and Donut (A, B, E, F, G). 'Odometer' and 'Thermometer' are not real ServiceNow report types, which is why they are excluded from the five correct answers.

questions.question: Which ServiceNow utility gives a service desk agent the ability to trace from a service having an issue, to see which CIs supporting that service have active issues?
questions.explanation: The CI Health Dashboard lets an agent start from a service and drill into the CIs supporting it to see which ones currently have active issues such as alerts, incidents, or changes (B). The Dependency View shows topology/relationships but is not the health-focused utility that surfaces which supporting CIs are unhealthy.

questions.question: On a related list, which buttons are commonly used for managing the records on the list? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Related lists commonly expose New (create a new related record), Edit (open the slushbucket to add/remove existing records), and Add for managing the records shown - B, C, E. 'Publish' and 'Manage' are not the standard related-list management buttons.

questions.question: A subject matter expert routinely receives tasks which have been worked by first level support, before receiving the assignment what could you suggest, to make it easier for the expert to read only the work notes in the activity log?
options: Click Context menu > Work Notes View
Click Personalize icon and select Activity Stream
Right click form header > Form Layout > Add Work Notes Section
Click Funnel icon and select only work notes
questions.explanation: The activity stream has a Funnel (filter) icon that lets you choose which activity types are displayed, so selecting only Work notes filters the stream down to just those entries (D). This is a per-user display filter; the other options describe form-layout or history actions that don't filter the activity stream to work notes only.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Filter the activity stream

questions.question: A task worker asks how they can monitor any updates occurring to records assigned to him, like responses from customers, what do you suggest?
options: Open an Agent workspace tab for each record he wants to monitor
Select Service Desk > My Work Dashboard
Click on the eyeglass icon to. expand the Monitor frame
On My Work list, select the Activity Stream icon to show a frame with live updates
questions.explanation: From the My Work list, the Activity Stream icon opens a live-updating frame that shows ongoing activity (such as customer responses) across the records, so the worker can monitor changes without opening each one (D). Opening a separate workspace tab per record is inefficient, and there is no 'Monitor frame' eyeglass feature as described in C.

questions.question: Which module would you use to customize your instances banner image, text and colors? A homepage admin > pages > branding
questions.explanation: The classic UI16 banner image, browser tab text, and system colors are configured under System Properties > Basic Configuration UI16, which centralizes the platform branding settings (C). The Service Portal branding option only themes a Service Portal, not the core platform UI banner, so it doesn't satisfy customizing the instance banner.

questions.question: What instance resource allows you to access guided tours, information about actions, and instructions on how to use inputs and outputs in your flow?
questions.explanation: The in-instance Help Panel, opened from the question-mark (?) icon, provides guided tours and contextual help - including guidance on actions and how to use inputs/outputs while building a flow (B). Community, Docs, and the Wiki are external resources, whereas the question asks about an in-instance resource embedded in the UI.

questions.question: Which feature enables business process owners to organize Flow Designer content into unified and digitized cross-enterprise processes via a digitized task board interface?
questions.explanation: Process Automation Designer (PAD) lets business process owners arrange Flow Designer flows into end-to-end, cross-enterprise processes using a visual lane/task-board interface (B). Flow Designer itself builds individual flows, and 'Process Workflow Designer' is not a real product name - PAD is the tool that orchestrates flows into a unified process.

questions.question: Which type of scripts run in the browser?
questions.explanation: Client-side logic - UI Policies and Client Scripts - executes in the user's browser, reacting to form events without a round-trip to the server. Access Control scripts, Script Includes, and Business Rules all run server-side, so they are not the scripts that execute in the browser.

questions.question: What are advantages of using spokes for integrations? (Choose three.)
options: Free spokes are available in the ServiceNow Store
questions.explanation: Spokes are packaged sets of Flow Designer actions for a given system, so they let you integrate with little or no code (A), are published as reusable, discoverable content (D), and can automate downstream work such as event handling (E). While many spokes are indeed free in the Store, that distribution detail is not counted as a core advantage here, and 'scale and control mechanisms' is not a defining spoke benefit.

questions.question: You have an existing customer, who is using workflows for their catalog items. Their existing purchasing policy is to require approval for any request that totals over 31000. However, management wants to change the approval threshold to 31500. Which workflow would you update to make this change?
questions.explanation: The out-of-box Service Catalog Request workflow runs against the Request (sc_request) record, where the order total lives, so the approval-threshold logic that compares the request total against a dollar amount is edited there. The other names are not the standard catalog re‐ quest workflow that evaluates the overall request total for approval.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Service Catalog request fulfillment

questions.question: How would you define an access control, to allow a user with iti role to have permission to create incident records?
options: Name: incident' ; Permission: write; Role: itil
Name: incident Any, Operation: write, Permission: itil
Name: incident.*; Operation: write; Permission: itil
Name: incident None, Permission: create: Role: itil
Name: incident. None; Operation: create; Role: itil
questions.explanation: Creating a record is governed by the 'create' operation, and a record-level (not field-level) ACL is written as table.None, so the rule that grants creation rights is incident.None with operation create and role itil (D). The 'write' operation controls editing existing records rather than inserting new ones, which is why the write-based options do not satisfy a 'create incident' requirement.

questions.question: What are the components that make up a filer condition? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Every condition (filter) row in ServiceNow is built from three parts: the Field to evaluate, the Operator that defines the comparison (is, contains, greater than, and so on), and the Value to compare against. 'Column' and 'Match Criteria' are not the named building blocks of a condition row, so C, D, and E are correct.

questions.question: You have been asked to create a way for users to order a new iphone, but only if they get two levels of approval. The approvers and users should be automatically notified at each approval level. What feature would you use to manage the approvals and notifications?
questions.explanation: A Flow Designer flow can model multi-stage approvals (request the first approval, then on success request the second) and send notifications to approvers and the requester at each stage, all in one declarative automation. Approval Criteria and Approver Delegates configure pieces of approval behavior but do not orchestrate sequential approval levels plus notifications the way a flow does.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Approvals in Flow Designer

questions.question: What is the language used for scriptingin ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: Server-side and client-side scripting in ServiceNow is done in JavaScript, with the server using the Rhino/embedded JavaScript engine via APIs like GlideRecord. C++, PHP, and Python are not the platform's scripting language, so JavaScript is the only correct choice.

questions.question: What access does a user need to be able to import articles to a knowledge base?
questions.explanation: Importing articles into a knowledge base is a content-authoring action, which requires 'Can contribute' access on that knowledge base; contributors can add and import articles, while read-only users (the 'Can read' criteria) cannot. The other options are not the access levels exposed by a knowledge base's User Criteria for contribution.

questions.question: Groups are stored in what table?
questions.explanation: Groups are stored in the Group table whose database name is sys_user_group (singular, with the sys_ prefix used for core platform tables). The plural and sn_-prefixed variants in the other options are not valid platform table names for groups.

questions.question: An it user calls the service desk because they need to work on task records. All they can see is self service on their homepage when they login to the ServiceNow instance. What issue could explain this? (Choose two.)
options: Their user account failed LDAP authentication
Their user account is not logged in properly
Their user account was not approved by their manager
Their user account does not have itil role
Their user account does not belong to any groups, which contain the itil role
questions.explanation: Seeing only Self Service means the user lacks the itil role that exposes the fulfiller applications and task records - either because the role was never granted directly (D) or because they are not in any group that carries the itil role (E), since roles can be inherited from group membership. LDAP failures would block login entirely, and ServiceNow has no per-user 'manager approval' gate for roles, so A and C do not explain the symptom.

questions.question: A service catalog project will involve building 80 catalog items. For each of the catalog items, the following fields will be mandatory on the forms: 'Requested for', 'Requested by', 'Approving manager', 'Delivery instructions'. All of the other variables will be specific to the individual catalog item. What features would you use when designing the catalog item form?
options: Create one Variable Set for the four variables; then add that variable set to each of the 80 catalog items.
Create a Record Producer that contains the four fields: then add to the record producer related list on the Catalog files.
Create a Flow Designer Action, with Variable Set Data Pill; then apply flow to all of the 80 catalog items.
Create an Order Guide, which includes all variables: then copy and hide variables as needed.
Create a Variable Set Template: then apply to all of the catalog items.
questions.explanation: A Variable Set is a reusable, modular group of variables you build once and attach to many catalog items, which is exactly what is needed to add the same four mandatory fields to all 80 items without rebuilding them each time (A). An Order Guide bundles multiple items into a single request and is not a mechanism for sharing common variables across item forms, so D does not fit.

questions.question: What are the steps for importing data using an import set?
options: Select source file; Run automap; Transform data; Clean up target table
Set up LDAP; Test map: Create update set; Run import: Apply update set
Identify source; Import transform map: Run transformer; Verity import
Load the data; Create transform map; Transform data; Clean up import table
questions.explanation: The standard import-set flow is: load the source data into a staging (import set) table, create a transform map that links source fields to target fields, run the transform to move the data into the target table, then clean up the staging import table (D). The other sequences mix in unrelated steps like LDAP setup or update sets, which are not part of the import-set process.

questions.question: To apply a UI policy to all views, which field should be set to true in its definition record?
questions.explanation: On the UI Policy definition record, the Global field controls whether the policy runs on every view of the table. Setting Global to true applies it to all views; clearing it lets you target a single view via the View field. Therefore the correct answer is D, not Inherit.

questions.question: You have heard about a new application released by ServiceNow, you want to try it out, to see if it might be useful for your company's ServiceNow implementation. What would be the best way to get hands-on experience with the new application?
options: Check the latest release notes at docs.servicenow.com.
Activate the application plug in, on your personal dev instance.
Search the wiki for the sales demo request form.
Activate the application plug in, on your company's production instance.
questions.explanation: A free personal developer instance is the safe sandbox for trying a new plugin hands-on without risking real data, so activating the plugin there lets you evaluate the application (B). Activating an unproven plugin directly on production (D) is risky and not a recommended way to experiment.

questions.question: On a business rule, the when salting determines at what point the rule executes. What are the options for specifying that timing?
questions.explanation: The Business Rule 'When' field offers Before, After, Async, and Display, which control whether the rule runs before/after the database write, asynchronously via a scheduled job, or when the record is loaded for display (B). Insert/Update/Delete/Query are the triggering operations (a separate setting), not the 'When' timing options.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Business rules (When to run)

questions.question: What icon do you use to change the boon and color on a favorite?
questions.explanation: After creating a Favorite you click the pencil (edit) icon to open its editor, where you can change the favorite's icon and color. The star icon creates/marks a favorite but does not open the editing controls for icon and color, so the pencil is the correct choice.

questions.question: What are examples of Ul actions, relating to lists? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: UI Actions that relate to lists are exposed through placements such as List link (A), List button (C), List context menu (D), and List choice (F). 'List Control' (B) is not a UI Action list placement, so the correct four are A, C, D, F.

questions.question: Which type of scripts run in the browser?
questions.explanation: UI Policies and Client Scripts are client-side and execute in the user's browser, manipulating the form without contacting the server. Script Includes, Business Rules, and Access Control scripts all run on the server, so D is the only set that runs in the browser.

questions.question: THE REPORT DESIGNER CONTAINS DIFFERENT SECTIONS FOR CONFIGURING YOUR REPORT. WHICH SECTION IS USED TO SPECIFY GROUPING AND CALCULATIONS TO BE RUN AGAINST ME DATA?
questions.explanation: In the Report Designer the Configure section is where you define how the data is grouped and what aggregations/calculations (such as count, sum, or average) are applied. The Data section chooses the source table and the report name, while Style controls visual appearance - neither sets up grouping and calculations.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Create a report (Report Designer)

questions.question: What role enables someone to authorize a request, with no other permissions on the platform?
questions.explanation: The approver_user role lets a user act on approvals - view and respond to approval requests - without granting any of the broader fulfiller permissions of itil. The other role names listed are not the standard approval role in ServiceNow, so Approver [approver_user] is the correct answer.

questions.question: What module do you use to access the reports that are available to you?
questions.explanation: The Reports > View / Run module opens the list of reports you can see and run, and is the standard entry point for accessing and launching existing reports. The other module paths are not the View/Run access point for the reporting application.

questions.question: What do you click when you have made modification to your report, and you want to see the results without saving?
questions.explanation: Clicking Run in the Report Designer re-renders the report with your current, unsaved changes so you can preview the results before deciding to save. There is no separate Execute, Try it, Test, or Preview button that does this, which is why Run is the correct action.

questions.question: Security rules are defined to restrict the permission of users from viewing and interacting with data. What are these security rules called?
questions.explanation: Access Control Rules (ACLs) are the row- and field-level security records that determine whether a user can read, write, create, or delete data based on roles and conditions. The source key here is 'C', but Access Control Rules (D) is the correct ServiceNow term for these security rules.

questions.question: Which is the base table of the configuration management database hierarchy?
questions.explanation: The Configuration Item hierarchy is rooted in the base table named cmdb, from which cmdb_ci and all specific CI classes extend. The other strings are not valid CMDB base table names, so cmdb (D) is correct.

questions.question: How would you describe the relationship between the incident and task table?
options: Incident table has a many to many relationships with the Task table.
Incident table has a one to much relationship with the Task table.
Incident table is extended from task table.
incident table is related to the Task table via the INC number
incident table is a database view of the Task table
questions.explanation: Incident is a child table that extends the Task [task] table, inheriting Task's fields (number, state, assignment group, and so on) through table inheritance. It is not a many-to-many relationship or a database view; the extension model is what links incident to task, making C correct.

questions.question: Which feature helps to automatically allocate a critical, high priority, service request to the appropriate assignment group or team member?
questions.explanation: Assignment Rules automatically set the assignment group and/or assigned-to on records that match defined conditions, which is exactly how a high-priority request is routed to the right team or person. UI Policy controls field behavior on forms and does not perform routing, so D is correct.

questions.question: What setting allows users to view a knowledge base article even if they are not logged in?
questions.explanation: Marking knowledge content as Public (via the 'Can Read' user criteria flagged public / the public knowledge base setting) lets unauthenticated visitors read articles without signing in. Roles like ESS require a logged-in user, so they cannot grant access to anonymous visitors, which is why the Public setting is correct.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Make a knowledge base public

questions.question: You are looking at a list of active incidents. You want to exclude incidents with the state of Resolved. How might you do that?
options: On the list of records, locate the right-click on the Resolved value, select Exclude.
Click Funnel icon, click AND, Select Resolved, is Not State click Run
On state column title, right-click, select Filter Out > Resolved
On Search, select State, type not Resolved, press enter
On the list of records, locate and right-click on the Resolved value, select Filter Out
questions.explanation: Right-clicking a specific cell value in a list and choosing 'Filter Out' adds a condition that excludes rows with that value, so right-clicking a Resolved value and selecting Filter Out removes the Resolved incidents (E). There is no 'Exclude' option on the value's context menu, and the column-title menu does not offer a per-value 'Filter Out > Resolved', which is why the other options are wrong.

questions.question: While showing a customer their incident form, they ask to change the priority field title to display their internal terminology pvalue. How would you do that? (Choose two.)
options: Right click on Priority and select Configure Dictionary
Right click on Priority and select Configure Display Settings
Right click on Priority and select Configure Label
Right click on Priority and select Configure Column
questions.explanation: A field's displayed title comes from its label, which you can change either by editing the dictionary entry (Configure Dictionary) or by editing the label directly (Configure Label) - both A and C update what users see. 'Configure Display Settings' and 'Configure Column' are not the ways to rename a field's label.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Change a field label

questions.question: Which testing framework is used to test servernew applications?
questions.explanation: The Automated Test Framework (ATF) is ServiceNow's built-in tool for creating and running automated tests against platform applications and upgrades. Selenium and JUnit are external, non-ServiceNow tools, so ATF (D) is the correct framework.

questions.question: The report designer contains different section for configuring your report. Which section is used to specify the name of the report, and the table or data source for the report.
questions.explanation: The Data section of the Report Designer is where you name the report and choose its source (a table, a data source, or another defined source). Configure handles grouping and aggregation, while Style/Type handle visualization choice - so the report name plus data source are set in the Data section.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Create a report (Data source)

questions.question: Which framework can automatically populate values for the priority and category field based on the short description field value?
questions.explanation: Predictive Intelligence uses machine-learning classification to read text such as the short description and automatically predict and populate fields like Category and Priority. Assignment Rules only set assignment fields based on static conditions and cannot interpret free-text, so the source key 'B' is incorrect and Predictive Intelligence (D) is the right framework.

questions.question: As administrator, what must you do to access feature of high security settings?
options: Add security_admin role to your user account
Use System Administrator < Elevate Roles module
questions.explanation: The security_admin role is an elevated privilege, so an admin who already has it temporarily activates it by choosing Elevate Roles from the user/settings menu before editing High Security Settings. You do not permanently add or impersonate the role for this; selecting Elevate Roles (A) is the documented step.

questions.question: A customer has asked for the following updates to a form: make 'Resolution code' mandatory, 'Admin State' is changed to 'Resolved'. Hide 'Major Incident' check box, unless logged in user has 'Major Incident Manager' role. What type of rules would you use to implement this requirement?
questions.explanation: Making a field mandatory based on another field's value and hiding a field based on the user's role are both client-side form behaviors, which is exactly what a UI Policy (optionally with a UI Policy script) does without coding. 'Dictionary Design', 'UI Design', 'Field Limiter', and 'Form Constraint' are not the standard mechanisms for these dynamic form rules, so UI Policy is correct.

questions.question: What framework can be used to manage the tables and CIs associated with a use case?
options: Common Service Date Model (CSDM) product view
questions.explanation: The Common Service Data Model (CSDM) provides the standard framework and product views that define which tables and CIs map to a given use case, guiding consistent CMDB data placement. The other named 'modeler/dashboard' tools are not the CSDM framework, so A is correct.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Common Service Data Model (CSDM)

questions.question: What is the name of the string that display filter criteria?
questions.explanation: The breadcrumb is the clickable string shown above a list that displays the applied filter conditions and lets you step back through them by removing the rightmost parts. 'Choice', 'Topic', and 'Menu' do not name this filter string, so Breadcrumb (C) is correct.

questions.question: A customer has asked for the following updates to a form: Make 'Resolution code' mandatory, 'Admin State' is changed to 'Resolved'. Hide 'Major Incident' check box, unless logged in user has 'Major Incident Manager' role. What type of rules would you use to implement this requirement?
questions.explanation: A UI Policy can make Resolution code mandatory when State is Resolved and hide the Major Incident checkbox unless the user has the Major Incident Manager role, all in one rule. 'Form Constraint' is not a real ServiceNow rule type, so the correct answer is C only.

questions.question: A new employee joins the it deployment and needs to perform work assigned to network and hardware groups. How would you set up their access? (Choose three.)
options: Add User Account to itll group
Add User Account to network group
Add User Account to IT Knowledgebase
Add User Account to Hardware group
questions.explanation: To give a new employee the right access you first create the user account (E), then add it to the Network group (C) and the Hardware group (F) so they inherit each group's roles and receive work assigned to those groups. You do not add a user 'to an ACL', so the source key 'B' is wrong; group membership is the correct mechanism.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Groups and group membership

questions.question: Which allows the creation of a task-based record from service catalog?
questions.explanation: A Record Producer is a catalog-style form that lets users create a record on a task-based table (such as incident or a custom task) directly from the Service Catalog. UI Builder, Assignment Rules, Flow Designer, and UI Actions do not provide that catalog-to-record creation, so Record Producers (A) is correct.

questions.question: THE CUSTOMER HAS ASKED THAT YOUR CHANGE THE DEFAULT LAYOUT OF THE TASK LIST. Number Task Type Parent Short Description Assignment Group Assignment Updated After navigation to the list, where would you click, to meet this requirement? Lists,
options: Right click on any column header, Context menu > Configure > List Layout
Right click List Gear icon > Configure > Columns
Click List Context Menu > Personalize List
Click List Context Menu > Configure Columns
questions.explanation: Changing the default columns of a list for all users is done through Configure > List Layout, reached by right-clicking a column header and using the context menu. 'Personalize List' only changes columns for the current user, and the other paths are not the standard route to the List Layout editor, so A is correct.

questions.question: HERE IS AN EXAMPLE OF THE CRITERIA SET FOR A KNOWLEDGE BASE: Companies: ACME North America Department: HR Groups: ACME Manager Match All: Yes In this example, what users would have access to this knowledge base?
options: Members of the ACME manager group, who are also members of HR Department and part of the ACME North America
Employees of ACME North America, who are members of HR Department or the ACME Manager group
Users which are members of either ACME North America, or HR Department, or ACME Manager Group
Member of the ACME Manager group, and HR department, regardless of geography
questions.explanation: When 'Match All' is set to Yes, the user criteria are combined with AND, so a user must satisfy every condition - be in ACME North America, in the HR department, and in the ACME Manager group - to gain access (A). The 'or' interpretations (B, C) describe Match All = No behavior, and D ignores the company condition.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Knowledge user criteria (Match All)

questions.question: What actions are taken to filter a long list of records to show only those which have 'email' short description?
options: Click List Magnifier to expand column search, on Short Description, type %email, click enter
Click List Magnifier to expand column search, on Short Description, type email, click enter
On Search box, select text, type email, click enter
Click List Magnifier to expand column search, on Short Description, type 'email, click enter
questions.explanation: Clicking the list magnifier opens the per-column search row, and entering text there filters that column; to match Short Descriptions that start with 'email', you prefix the term so the search anchors the leading characters. The source key is D, though in practice the plain 'contains' search (option B) is the most common way to find any record whose Short Description includes 'email'.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Search a list column

questions.question: Which data consistency settings can be achieved using UI policy? (Choose three.)
options: Setting fields to accept the data with a number of characters
Setting fields to accept the data in an expected format
questions.explanation: A UI Policy can dynamically make fields hidden (B), read-only (D), and mandatory (E) on the form, which helps enforce data consistency at entry time. Limiting character length or enforcing a specific input format are dictionary/validation concerns, not UI Policy actions, so A and C are excluded.

questions.question: An it user calls the service desk because his work needs to be completed on ask records. All he can see a self service on his homepage when he Logs in to the ServiceNow instance. What issue could explain this? (Choose two.)
options: His user account failed LDAP authentication
His user account does not Belong to any groups, which contain the ITIL role
His user account was not approved by his manager
His user account does not have ITIL role
His user account Is not logged in properly
questions.explanation: Only seeing Self Service indicates the user is missing the itil role, which is granted either directly (D) or by membership in a group that carries it (B); without it, the fulfiller apps and task records stay hidden. A failed LDAP login would prevent access entirely and a 'manager approval' gate does not exist for roles, so those options do not explain the symptom.

questions.question: From an open form, you click the Form Context menu (the icon at the top-left of the form header), which lists options such as Save, Configure, Export, View, Create Favorite, Copy URL, Show XML, History, and Reload Form. Which path from this menu opens the table configuration page?
options: The Form Context menu > View > Table
The Form Context menu > Configure > Table
The Form Context menu > Configure > Dictionary
The Form Context menu > View > Show Table
questions.explanation: From any form, open the Form Context menu (the icon at the top-left of the form header) and choose Configure > Table to open that table's configuration record. Configure > Dictionary edits the dictionary entry for a single field rather than the whole table, and the View submenu only changes how the current record is displayed - it does not open table configuration.

questions.question: A customer wants to use a client script to validate things on a form in order to make sure the submission makes sense. What type of client script would you recommend to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: An onSubmit client script runs the moment the user submits the form, which is exactly when you validate that the entered data makes sense - returning false cancels the submission if a check fails. onLoad runs when the form first loads (too early to validate input), and onSubmission()/onUpdate() are not valid ServiceNow client script types.

questions.question: What action will allow you to personalize layouts of columns in a list?
options: Click Gear icon > Personalize window options > Select the appropriate columns
Select the column to be personalized > Click Edit icon (Penal) > Choose me options to personage
Select the column to be personalized and right at the header > Choose the options to personalize
questions.explanation: To choose which columns appear in a list, click the list's gear (Personalize List) icon, which opens the Personalize List Columns slushbucket where you move fields between Available and Selected (A). The other options describe garbled or non-existent paths; personalization of which columns show is driven from the gear icon, not by clicking individual column edit pencils.

questions.question: An order placed through the service catalog creates two records in the platform for the newly ordered item. Which two records are these? (Choose two.)
options: A record in the sc_task table
A record in the sc_req_item table
questions.explanation: Ordering a catalog item generates a Requested Item record (sc_req_item) for the line item itself and one or more Catalog Task records (sc_task) that fulfillers complete (A and B). Change, incident, and problem records belong to other ITSM processes and are not created automatically by placing a catalog order.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Service Catalog request fulfillment

questions.question: Which admin role is required to make changes to high security settings?
questions.explanation: Changing High Security Settings (the system security properties page) requires the elevated security_admin role, which a user temporarily activates via Elevate Roles (A). The base admin role alone cannot edit these settings, and sn_ad_admin and high_sec_admin are not the roles that gate high-security configuration.

questions.question: What component of the ServiceNow infrastructure defines every table and field in the system?
questions.explanation: The Data Dictionary (sys_dictionary) defines every table and every field in the platform, including each field's type, length, and attributes (D). A schema map is a visualization of table relationships, not the definition store, and the other choices are not real ServiceNow components.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Tables and the data dictionary

questions.question: An order for new Office equipment has men placed through the service catalog. How would you view the lists of requests after the orders have men placed?
options: All > Service Catalog > Open Records > Items
In the Navigation Filter, type 'requests. Let' and press the Enter key.
questions.explanation: Submitted catalog orders are viewed by navigating through the Service Catalog application's Open Records modules to the Items list, where requested items appear (A). The garbled navigation-filter and 'Tables and Columns' paths are not valid ways to reach the request lists.

questions.question: Roles can inherit permissions from other roles. Which role inherits all of the permissions of the catalog role and the user_critena_admm role plus has permissions to create items and services?
questions.explanation: The Catalog Admin role (catalog_admin) contains the catalog and user_criteria_admin roles and adds the ability to create and manage catalog Items and Services (C). The catalog_write/author role can author items but lacks full administrative inheritance, and sys_admin is the general platform admin rather than the catalog-specific administrator described.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Service Catalog base system roles

questions.question: If users would like to locate and assign a task to themselves in the platform, what action could they perform from the list view to make the assignment? (Choose two.)
options: Select the record using the check box, then select the Person icon
Double click on the Assigned to value, type the name of the user, and select the green check
Select the record using the check box then select the Assign To Me UI action on the List Header
Right click on the Task number and select the Assign to me option in the menu
Select the Task number, and select the Assign to me UI action on the form
questions.explanation: A user can right-click a task's number in the list and choose Assign to me from the context menu (D), or open the task and click the Assign to me UI action on the form (E). There is no 'Person icon' assignment, and Assign to me is a record-level action rather than a list-header button, so A and C are incorrect.

questions.question: What actions are taken to filter a long list of records to show only those with the category of hardware?
options: On Breadcrumb, click the > icon, type Hardware and click enter
On the Category column header, right-click and select Show > Hardware
On the list, locate and right-click on the value Hardware, select Show Matching
Right-click on magnifier type Hardware and click enter
Click Funnel icon, type Hardware and click enter
questions.explanation: Right-clicking a cell value such as 'Hardware' and choosing Show Matching instantly filters the list to only rows sharing that value (C). 'Filter Out' would do the opposite. The other options describe controls (breadcrumb >, a column 'Show' submenu, the magnifier) that do not perform this one-click contextual filter.

questions.question: What section on a task record is used to see the most recent updates made to a record?
questions.explanation: The Activity Stream (activity formatter) on a task form chronologically shows the most recent updates - field changes, comments, and work notes (B). Related Lists display associated records, and while auditing tracks history behind the scenes, the on-form section users read for recent activity is the Activity Stream, not an 'Audit Log' or 'Timeline' section.

questions.question: After finishing your work on high security settings, what is a possible way to return to normal admin security levels?
options: Use System Administration > Normal Security module
questions.explanation: The security_admin role needed for High Security Settings is an elevated privilege that persists only for the current login session. It is released automatically by session timeout or by logging out, so logging out and back in (C) returns the user to normal administrator privileges. The 'Normal Security' module in option A does not exist in the base instance.

questions.question: Access control rules are applied to a specific table, like the incident table. What is the object name for a rule that applies to the entire incident table (All rows and fields)?
questions.explanation: An ACL is named table.field, and using the wildcard * for the field - incident.* - applies the rule to every field on every row of the Incident table (A). '.all', '.!', and '.None' are not valid ACL field tokens; the asterisk is the wildcard that means 'all fields'.

questions.question: On a list, what does each row show?
questions.explanation: A list displays the records from a table, with each row representing one record (B) and each column representing a field on that table. The list as a whole is the view of the table, so 'a table' and 'a field' describe the wrong granularity, and a filter merely narrows which rows appear.

questions.question: Which action enables personalization in a form for the admin role, only?
options: Navigate to sys_form_properties.list and set the property glide.ui.enable_personalize_form.admin to true.
Navigate to Context Menu > Configure > Form Layout and select 'Enable Personalization' and Enter the 'admin' role.
Navigate to Context Menu > Configure > Table and add the role 'Admin' in the 'Available User' list box.
Navigate to sys_properties.list find the property glide.ui.personalize_form.role and set the Value to admin.
questions.explanation: Restricting the Personalize Form capability to a single role is done with the system property glide.ui.personalize_form.role, set to admin via sys_properties.list (D). The property names and form-layout/table paths in the other options are not the supported mechanism for limiting personalization to the admin role.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Form administration and personalization

questions.question: Which element is used to track items not saved with a field, in a record?
questions.explanation: The Activity formatter (the activity stream) tracks information that is not stored in a single editable field, such as journal entries like comments and work notes, plus a running history of field changes (C). The List Editor edits field values inline, and the Dictionary defines fields - neither captures this activity history.

questions.question: What does ServiceNow recommend as a best practice regarding data imports?
options: Adjust your Transform maps, after the data is loaded into the target table.
Use extremely large Import Sets, instead of multiple large Import Sets.
Create a new Import set table for each new data load.
Plan time before your import to remove obsolete or inaccurate data.
Monitor data quality and clean imported data, using the Data Scrub Workspace.
questions.explanation: ServiceNow recommends cleansing source data before importing - planning time to remove obsolete or inaccurate records reduces the volume transformed and improves data quality (D). Reusing import set tables and configuring transform maps before loading are preferred over per-load tables and post-load tweaks, and there is no 'Data Scrub Workspace' product.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Import sets best practices

questions.question: When an administrator sets a policy that is applied to all data entered into the platform (UI, import sets, or web services), where does this policy run by default?
questions.explanation: A policy that governs all data regardless of entry channel - UI, Import Sets, or Web Services - is a Data Policy, and because those channels include non-UI paths it must run on the server (B). Client-side enforcement (browser) only applies to the form UI, so it cannot cover import or webservice data.

questions.question: If a user is on an incident form and is alerted when they change the value of the priority field, which type of script executes in the platform?
questions.explanation: Logic that reacts to a field value changing on a loaded form and alerts the user runs in the browser as a Client Script - specifically an onChange script on the Priority field (B). Business rules and server scripts execute on the server during database operations, and a fix script is a one-time maintenance script, none of which respond to live form-field changes.

questions.question: Which feature can be used to categorize a set of records from a list and make them visible to other users?
questions.explanation: Tags are labels you apply to records to categorize, filter, and find them, and a tag can be shared so it is visible to other users or groups (A). Favorites are personal navigation shortcuts, History shows recently visited records, and the Activity Formatter displays record updates - none of which categorize records for sharing.

questions.question: The testing team needs to be able to perform activities in the test instance, as though they are a member of the service desk group. What role would they need to be able to switch between user accounts, without logging out and back in?
questions.explanation: The impersonator role lets a user impersonate other accounts and act as them without logging out and back in, which is ideal for testing how the application behaves for different users (B). The service_desk role only grants Service Desk permissions, admin is broader than required, and 'incognito' is not a ServiceNow role.

questions.question: Which tables are available by default in a ServiceNow instance? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: User (sys_user), Incident, and Task are core platform tables present in every baseline instance (A, B, F). 'Item', 'Issue', and 'Project' are not baseline core tables - Project, for example, requires the PPM/SPM application - so they are not available by default.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Core tables (Task, User, Incident)

questions.question: An administrator creates "customer_table_admin" and "customer_table_user" roles for the newly created "customer table". Which ACL rule would grant access to all rows and all fields to both the customer_table_admin and customer_table_user roles?
questions.explanation: An ACL written as table.field with the wildcard * - customer.* - matches every field on every row of the Customer table, granting both roles broad access (B). '.all', '.field', and '.none' are not valid ACL field tokens; the asterisk wildcard is what represents 'all fields'.

questions.question: What contains the configuration changes made in an instance (I.e. Changes in a form) and helps to implement the changes from the dev environment to another environment?
questions.explanation: Update Sets capture configuration changes - form layouts, UI actions, business rules, workflows, and other customizations - into a package that can be exported from Dev and applied to Test or Prod (A). Transform maps and import sets move data, not configuration, and the system dictionary defines table/field structure rather than packaging changes for migration.

questions.question: Which set of steps is used to import spreadsheet data into a ServiceNow table?
options: Load Data, Create Transform Map, Run Transform
Select Import Set, Select Transform Map, Run Transform
Define Data Source, Select Transform Map, Run Transform
questions.explanation: The standard import flow is to Load Data from the spreadsheet into a staging import set table, Create a Transform Map that aligns source columns to target fields, then Run Transform to write the records into the target table (A). The other sequences skip the load step or assume artifacts (an existing import set or transform map) that have not been created yet.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Import a spreadsheet / import sets

questions.question: What process allows users to create, categorize, review approve and browse important information in a centralized location that is shared oy the entire organization?
questions.explanation: Knowledge Management is the process for creating, categorizing, reviewing, approving, and browsing articles in centralized knowledge bases shared across the organization (B). 'Knowledge-Centered' service is a methodology rather than the ServiceNow process named here, and the other options are not ServiceNow processes.

questions.question: A colleague wants to rearrange the columns on their my work list. Once the user has navigated to the list where should they navigate to select and arrange the columns?
options: Right click on any column header. Context Menu > Configure > List Layout
Click List Context Menu > Personalize List
Click List Content Menu > Configure > List Layout
questions.explanation: To rearrange list columns, right-click any column header and choose Configure > List Layout, which opens the slushbucket to add, remove, and reorder fields (B). The other options use nonexistent menu names ('List Content Menu') or refer to personalization that controls only column visibility for the individual user rather than the full list layout.

questions.question: Which feature ensures data consistency white importing data using import sets and web services?
questions.explanation: Data Policies enforce mandatory and read-only field rules on the server for all data entry channels, including import sets and web services, ensuring consistency regardless of source (C). Client Scripts and UI Policies act only on the form in the browser, so they cannot govern non-UI imports.

questions.question: Which low components allow you to specify when a flow should be run?
questions.explanation: A flow's Trigger defines the event that starts it, and the Condition narrows that to the specific circumstances under which it should actually run, so together they specify when a flow runs (C). The other pairings mix in unrelated terms like Scope, Clock, and Table that are not what controls flow execution timing.

questions.question: When using Flow Designer what is the flow execution initiated by?
questions.explanation: A flow's execution is initiated by its Trigger, which specifies the condition that starts the flow - a record being created or updated, a schedule, an inbound email, or an SLA target (A). Subflows are reusable logic called from within flows, and data pills carry values between steps; neither starts the flow.

questions.question: Which system property is added and set to true in order to see impersonation events in the system log?
questions.explanation: Adding the system property glide.sys.log_impersonation and setting it to true causes impersonation start/stop events to be written to the Event log, viewable under System Logs (C). The other property names are fabricated and do not control impersonation logging.

questions.question: A customer wants to be able to identify and track components of their infrastructure that support their ecommerce service. What ServiceNow products could support this requirement? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The CMDB stores configuration items and their relationships as the single source of truth for infrastructure, Discovery automatically scans the network to populate the CMDB, and Service Mapping builds a top-down view of the CIs that support a specific business service such as ecommerce (B, D, E). Performance Analytics and Financial Management address trending and cost, not infrastructure discovery and mapping.

questions.question: You are editing a new incident record and want the save button to appear on the form header. Which action makes that button appear?
options: All > System Properties > UI Properties > turn on the glide.ui.advanced property
Context Menu > Form Design > add the Save button
All > System Properties > UI Properties > turn on the Save button
Context Menu > Form Layout > add the Save button
questions.explanation: Displaying a Save button in the form header is controlled by a UI property (glide.ui.save_button), which an administrator turns on via System Properties > UI Properties (C). Form Design and Form Layout configure which fields appear on the form, not whether the header Save button is shown.

questions.question: Which tables are children of the Task table and come with the base system? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Incident, Problem, and Change Request all extend the Task (task) table in the baseline platform, inheriting its fields and adding their own (A, B, C). The Dictionary and CMDB are not children of Task - CMDB tables extend cmdb_ci - and 'Config' is not a baseline Task child table.

questions.question: What are the benefits of building flows using Flow Designer? (Choose three.)
options: Supports easy integration with 3rd party systems
Provides natural-language descriptions of flow logic
Provides built-in libraries /API for complex coding
questions.explanation: Flow Designer integrates with third-party systems through Integration Hub spokes, presents flow logic in natural language so non-developers can read it, and enables no-code automation via a visual builder and prebuilt actions (A, C, D). Its value is the no/low-code approach, so 'IDE for complicated scripting' and 'built-in libraries for complex coding' run counter to its purpose, and it does not auto-populate SLA records.

questions.question: Which helps to visualize configuration items and their relationships?
questions.explanation: The Dependency View (CI relationship map) visually displays configuration items and how they relate, letting you see connections and assess the impact of changes on dependent CIs (E). A Schema Map diagrams table/field structure rather than CI relationships, and Transform Maps and Flow Designer serve unrelated purposes.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - CI relationships / Dependency View

questions.question: What component causes a flow to run after a record has been created or updated?
questions.explanation: A Record-based trigger (Created, Updated, or Created or Updated) starts a flow when a record changes in a specified table, evaluating conditions against the record's values (B). Date-based triggers fire on a schedule relative to a date field, and 'On-change', 'Application-based', and 'Updated-date' are not the names of the record trigger type in Flow Designer.
questions.reference: ServiceNow Docs - Flow Designer trigger types
